subject: Genesis
question: What new name does Jacob receive after his wrestling at the ford of the Jabbok?
explanation: “Thy name shall be called no more Jacob, but Israel: for thou hast struggled with God and with men.” Edom is Esau’s nickname (36:1).

subject: Genesis
question: How old was Abram when he left Haran for Canaan?
explanation: “Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.” He was 86 at the birth of Ishmael (16:16) and 100 at the birth of Isaac (21:5).

subject: Genesis
question: How many years in all did Jacob spend serving Laban?
explanation: “Thus have I been twenty years in thy house; I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle.”

subject: Genesis
question: How long did the rain of the flood fall on the earth?
explanation: “The rain was upon the earth forty days and forty nights.” The hundred and fifty days are the time the waters prevailed upon the earth (7:24).

subject: Exodus
question: Where were the Israelites to put the blood of the Passover lamb?
choice_a: On the altar in the middle of the camp
choice_b: On the foreheads of the firstborn
choice_c: On the two side posts and the lintel of the door
choice_d: On the threshold of the house
answer_text: On the two side posts and the lintel of the door
explanation: “They shall take of the blood, and strike it on the two side posts and on the upper door post of the houses, wherein they shall eat it.”

subject: Exodus
question: Who advised Moses to appoint rulers of thousands, hundreds, fifties and tens to judge the people?
explanation: His father-in-law said to him: “The thing that thou doest is not good… provide out of all the people able men, such as fear God,” and appoint them as rulers.

subject: Exodus
question: What were the names of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God rather than Pharaoh?
explanation: The Hebrew midwives, “of which the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah,” “feared God” and let the children live.

subject: Exodus
question: What name does God reveal to Moses at the burning bush?
explanation: “I AM THAT I AM… I AM hath sent me unto you.” “The LORD is my banner” is the name of the altar built after the victory over Amalek (17:15).

subject: Leviticus
question: What did Nadab and Abihu bring before the LORD, which caused their death?
explanation: “They offered strange fire before the LORD, which he commanded them not. And there went out fire from the LORD, and devoured them.”

subject: Leviticus
question: On what date did the Day of Atonement take place?
choice_a: The fourteenth day of the first month
choice_b: The first day of the seventh month
choice_c: The fifteenth day of the seventh month
choice_d: The tenth day of the seventh month
answer_text: The tenth day of the seventh month
explanation: “In the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month, ye shall afflict your souls.” The 14th of the first month is Passover (23:5), the 15th of the seventh the Feast of Tabernacles (23:34).

subject: Leviticus
question: At the consecration of Aaron, where did Moses put the blood of the ram?
choice_a: On the forehead, the chest and both hands
choice_b: On the four horns of the altar only
choice_c: On the breastplate and on Aaron’s turban
choice_d: On the right ear, thumb and big toe
answer_text: On the right ear, thumb and big toe
explanation: Moses put blood “upon the tip of Aaron’s right ear, and upon the thumb of his right hand, and upon the great toe of his right foot.”

subject: Leviticus
question: Which year was proclaimed the year of jubilee, when everyone returned to his property?
explanation: “Ye shall hallow the fiftieth year… it shall be a jubilee unto you; and ye shall return every man unto his possession.” The seventh year is the sabbatical year (25:4).

subject: Numbers
question: Which two spies encouraged the people to enter Canaan?
explanation: Joshua the son of Nun and Caleb the son of Jephunneh rent their clothes and said: “The land, which we passed through to search it, is an exceeding good land.”

subject: Numbers
question: Who joined Korah in rebelling against Moses?
explanation: Korah took men, “and Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, and On, the son of Peleth,” and rose up before Moses with two hundred and fifty princes of the assembly.

subject: Numbers
question: Complete Balaam’s oracle: “There shall come a Star out of Jacob, …”
choice_a: and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel
choice_b: and a Branch shall grow out of the stem of Jesse
choice_c: and a lion’s whelp shall rise out of Judah
choice_d: and a light shall shine upon Zion
answer_text: and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel
explanation: “I shall see him, but not now… there shall come a Star out of Jacob, and a Sceptre shall rise out of Israel, and shall smite the corners of Moab.”

subject: Numbers
question: Which animal spoke to Balaam on the road?
explanation: “The LORD opened the mouth of the ass, and she said unto Balaam, What have I done unto thee, that thou hast smitten me these three times?”

subject: Deuteronomy
question: On which mountain did Moses climb to see the promised land before he died?
explanation: “Moses went up from the plains of Moab unto the mountain of Nebo, to the top of Pisgah”; the LORD showed him all the land, and he died there. Aaron, for his part, died on Mount Hor.

subject: Deuteronomy
question: According to the law of the king, what was the king to do when he sat on the throne?
choice_b: Write a copy of the law and read it every day
choice_c: Offer a thousand burnt offerings to the LORD
choice_d: Build a house for the ark of God
answer_text: Write a copy of the law and read it every day
explanation: “He shall write him a copy of this law in a book… And it shall be with him, and he shall read therein all the days of his life.”

subject: Deuteronomy
question: How often was the law to be read before all Israel, and at which feast?
choice_b: Every three years, at the Feast of Weeks
choice_c: Every seven years, at the Feast of Tabernacles
choice_d: Every fifty years, at the jubilee
answer_text: Every seven years, at the Feast of Tabernacles
explanation: “At the end of every seven years, in the solemnity of the year of release, in the feast of tabernacles… thou shalt read this law before all Israel in their hearing.”

subject: Deuteronomy
question: Complete: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God …”
choice_b: is a great God and a terrible
explanation: “Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God is one LORD: and thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thine heart…”

subject: Joshua
question: How many times did the Israelites march around Jericho on the seventh day?
explanation: On the first six days, once a day; “on the seventh day… they compassed the city after the same manner seven times.”

subject: Joshua
question: How old was Caleb when he asked for the hill country of Hebron?
explanation: “I am this day fourscore and five years old. As yet I am as strong this day… Now therefore give me this mountain.”

subject: Joshua
question: How many defeated kings are listed in Joshua 12?
explanation: The list ends with the king of Tirzah: “all the kings thirty and one.”

subject: Joshua
question: Complete Joshua’s declaration at Shechem: “As for me and my house, we will …”
explanation: “Choose you this day whom ye will serve… but as for me and my house, we will serve the LORD.”

subject: Judges
question: Who got the secret of Samson’s strength out of him and betrayed him to the Philistines?
explanation: Delilah, seeing that he had told her all his heart, called for the lords of the Philistines, and then had Samson’s seven locks shaved.

subject: Judges
question: How did Sisera, commander of Jabin’s army, die?
choice_a: Barak ran him through at the brook Kishon
choice_b: Jael drove a tent peg through his temple
choice_c: A woman dropped a millstone on his head
choice_d: He drowned in the brook with his chariots
answer_text: Jael drove a tent peg through his temple
explanation: Sisera was sleeping in the tent; Jael, the wife of Heber, “smote the nail into his temples, and fastened it into the ground.” The millstone was Abimelech’s death.

subject: Judges
question: In Jotham’s fable, which tree agrees to reign over the others?
explanation: The trees finally said to the bramble, “Come thou, and reign over us”; it agreed, threatening to devour the cedars of Lebanon.

subject: Judges
question: With how many men did Gideon attack the camp of Midian?
explanation: Those who lapped the water numbered three hundred, and the LORD said: “By the three hundred men that lapped will I save you.”

subject: Ruth
question: In whose field does Ruth go to glean?
explanation: “Her hap was to light on a part of the field belonging unto Boaz, who was of the kindred of Elimelech.”

subject: Ruth
question: Why do Elimelech and his family leave Bethlehem?
explanation: “In the days when the judges ruled, … there was a famine in the land,” and the man of Bethlehem went to sojourn in the country of Moab.

subject: Ruth
question: How many elders does Boaz seat at the city gate to settle the matter?
explanation: “He took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, Sit ye down here.”

subject: Ruth
question: What is the relationship between Obed, Ruth’s son, and King David?
explanation: Obed “is the father of Jesse, the father of David”: he is therefore David’s grandfather, not his great-grandfather (that is Boaz).

subject: 1 Samuel
question: What does David use to bring down Goliath?
explanation: “David prevailed over the Philistine with a sling and with a stone… but there was no sword in the hand of David.” He had refused Saul’s armor.

subject: 1 Samuel
question: Which dead man does Saul ask the woman of Endor to bring up?
explanation: The woman asks: “Whom shall I bring up unto thee?” Saul answers: “Bring me up Samuel.”

subject: 1 Samuel
question: What name does Eli’s daughter-in-law give to the child born on the day the ark was captured?
explanation: She named him Ichabod, saying, “The glory is departed from Israel,” because the ark of God was taken and because of the deaths of her father-in-law and her husband.

subject: 1 Samuel
question: What is the name of Samuel’s mother?
explanation: Hannah, one of Elkanah’s two wives, conceived and bore a son whom she named Samuel: “Because I have asked him of the LORD.” Peninnah was Elkanah’s other wife.

subject: 2 Samuel
question: How old is David when he becomes king, and how many years does he reign?
explanation: “David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned forty years.” The thirty-three years are the length of his reign at Jerusalem.

subject: 2 Samuel
question: Who is Mephibosheth, whom David has eat at his table?
explanation: “Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan, the son of Saul”; David tells him, “thou shalt eat bread at my table continually.” Ziba was the servant of the house of Saul.

subject: 2 Samuel
question: How many men does the plague kill in Israel after the census?
explanation: David chooses to fall into the hand of the LORD; “from Dan even to Beer-sheba seventy thousand men” of the people died.

subject: 2 Samuel
question: In which city is David first anointed king over the house of Judah?
explanation: The LORD answers David: “Unto Hebron.” The men of Judah came, “and there they anointed David king over the house of Judah.”

subject: 1 Kings
question: Which queen comes to test Solomon with hard questions?
explanation: “When the queen of Sheba heard of the fame of Solomon … she came to prove him with hard questions.”

subject: 1 Kings
question: In which cities does Jeroboam place the two golden calves?
explanation: After making two calves of gold, “he set the one in Beth-el, and the other put he in Dan.”

subject: 1 Kings
question: How long does Zimri reign over Israel?
explanation: “Zimri reign[ed] seven days in Tirzah.” When he saw that the city was taken, he burned the king’s house down over himself.

subject: 1 Kings
question: Which king of Tyre supplies Solomon with the cedars of Lebanon for the temple?
explanation: Hiram sent word: “I will do all thy desire concerning timber of cedar, and concerning timber of fir,” and his servants brought the logs down from Lebanon.

subject: 2 Kings
question: Under which king of Babylon is Jerusalem taken and the temple burned?
explanation: In the nineteenth year of King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon, Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, “burnt the house of the LORD.”

subject: 2 Kings
question: What does the high priest Hilkiah find in the temple under Josiah?
explanation: Hilkiah says to Shaphan: “I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD,” and Shaphan read it.

subject: 2 Kings
question: Which prophetess do Josiah’s envoys consult about the book of the law?
explanation: Hilkiah and the others “went unto Huldah the prophetess, the wife of Shallum … (now she dwelt in Jerusalem).”

subject: 2 Kings
question: How does Elijah leave the earth?
choice_b: He disappears into the wilderness of Horeb
choice_c: He goes up to heaven in a whirlwind
choice_d: He is buried by Elisha at Gilgal
answer_text: He goes up to heaven in a whirlwind
explanation: A chariot of fire and horses of fire parted them both asunder, “and Elijah went up by a whirlwind into heaven.”

subject: 1 Chronicles
question: To whom does God entrust the building of the temple?
explanation: David repeats God’s word: “Solomon thy son, he shall build my house and my courts: for I have chosen him to be my son.”

subject: 1 Chronicles
question: How does God show that he accepts the altar David built on Ornan’s threshing floor?
choice_a: By a cloud that filled the threshing floor
choice_d: By fire coming down from heaven
answer_text: By fire coming down from heaven
explanation: David called on the LORD, “and he answered him from heaven by fire upon the altar of burnt offering.”

subject: 1 Chronicles
question: Into how many divisions are the priests divided by lot?
explanation: The lots run from the first, Jehoiarib, to “the four and twentieth to Maaziah”: that makes twenty-four divisions.

subject: 1 Chronicles
question: Which name do the genealogies of 1 Chronicles begin with?
explanation: The book opens right away with the list “Adam, Sheth, Enosh, Kenan…”, long before Noah and Abraham.

subject: 2 Chronicles
question: Which king of Persia allows the Jews to go up and rebuild the house of God?
explanation: “The LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus king of Persia,” who proclaimed: “Who is there among you of all his people?… let him go up.”

subject: 2 Chronicles
question: Why is King Uzziah struck with leprosy?
choice_a: He consulted physicians, not the LORD
choice_b: He sacrificed to the gods of Damascus
choice_d: He tried to burn incense on the altar
answer_text: He tried to burn incense on the altar
explanation: His heart was lifted up: he entered the temple to burn incense, a right reserved for the sons of Aaron, and leprosy broke out on his forehead.

subject: 2 Chronicles
question: According to Hanani the seer, why do the eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth?
choice_a: To look for a king after his own heart
choice_b: To strengthen those whose heart is wholly his
choice_c: To count the righteous in every nation
choice_d: To judge the nations that worship idols
answer_text: To strengthen those whose heart is wholly his
explanation: “The eyes of the LORD run to and fro throughout the whole earth, to show himself strong in the behalf of them whose heart is perfect toward him.”

subject: 2 Chronicles
question: On which mountain does Solomon build the temple?
explanation: Solomon builds “in mount Moriah,” in the place that David had prepared on the threshingfloor of Ornan the Jebusite.

subject: Ezra
question: Which prophets restart the building of the temple after the work was halted?
explanation: “Haggai the prophet, and Zechariah the son of Iddo, prophesied,” and then Zerubbabel and Jeshua rose up and began to build.

subject: Ezra
question: What happens as the foundations of the temple are laid?
choice_a: Fire falls from heaven on the altar
choice_b: The old men weep while others shout for joy
choice_c: Enemies of Judah attack the building site at night
choice_d: King Cyrus comes to attend the ceremony
answer_text: The old men weep while others shout for joy
explanation: The old men who had seen the first house wept with a loud voice, “so that the people could not discern the noise of the shout of joy from the noise of the weeping of the people.”

subject: Ezra
question: How long does Ezra’s journey from Babylon to Jerusalem take?
explanation: “Upon the first day of the first month began he to go up from Babylon, and on the first day of the fifth month came he to Jerusalem.”

subject: Ezra
question: Which Persian king issues the edict allowing the Jews to return to Jerusalem?
explanation: “In the first year of Cyrus king of Persia… the LORD stirred up the spirit of Cyrus,” who proclaimed: “Who is there among you of all his people? his God be with him, and let him go up to Jerusalem.”

subject: Nehemiah
question: What position does Nehemiah hold with King Artaxerxes?
explanation: Nehemiah ends his prayer with these words: “For I was the king’s cupbearer”; it was he who served the king his wine.

subject: Nehemiah
question: How is Jerusalem repopulated in chapter 11?
choice_a: The king sends Persian colonists there
choice_b: One person in ten is chosen by lot
choice_c: All the Levites are required to move there
answer_text: One person in ten is chosen by lot
explanation: “The rest of the people also cast lots, to bring one of ten to dwell in Jerusalem,” and the volunteers were blessed.

subject: Nehemiah
question: Who set Tobiah up in a room of the temple while Nehemiah was away?
explanation: “Eliashib the priest… was allied unto Tobiah: and he had prepared for him a great chamber,” where the offerings used to be stored.

subject: Nehemiah
question: Who reads the book of the law before all the people in chapter 8?
explanation: Ezra the priest brought the law before the congregation and read from it from morning until midday, standing on a wooden platform made for the purpose.

subject: Esther
question: On what was Haman finally hanged?
choice_d: A great tree in the palace garden
explanation: At Harbona’s word, the king said, “Hang him thereon. So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai.”

subject: Esther
question: Why could the king not simply cancel Haman’s decree?
choice_a: Haman had already had it carried out everywhere
choice_b: The seven princes of Persia and Media opposed it
choice_c: A decree sealed with the king’s ring is irreversible
choice_d: The decree had been voted by the people
answer_text: A decree sealed with the king’s ring is irreversible
explanation: “The writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may no man reverse”: a second decree had to be written.

subject: Esther
question: On what days is the feast of Purim celebrated?
choice_a: The 14th and 15th of the month Adar
choice_d: The 1st and 10th of the seventh month
answer_text: The 14th and 15th of the month Adar
explanation: Mordecai prescribes “that they should keep the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and the fifteenth day of the same, yearly.”

subject: Esther
question: What does the word “Pur,” which gave the feast of Purim its name, mean?
explanation: Before Haman, “they cast Pur, that is, the lot,” to fix the day of the massacre; hence the name Purim.

subject: Job
question: In which land did Job live?
explanation: “There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job.” Teman is the city of Eliphaz, one of his three friends.

subject: Job
question: Who are the three friends who come to comfort Job?
explanation: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite come to mourn with him and comfort him; Elihu does not speak until chapter 32.

subject: Job
question: After his restoration, how many sons and daughters does Job have?
explanation: His livestock is doubled (fourteen thousand sheep instead of seven thousand), but he again has “seven sons and three daughters.”

subject: Job
question: Where does the LORD speak to Job from?
explanation: “Then the LORD answered Job out of the whirlwind, and said…”: from there he questions him about creation.

subject: Psalms
question: Which word opens the first psalm?
explanation: The book opens with “Blessed is the man that walketh not in the counsel of the ungodly.” “Why” opens Psalm 2.

subject: Psalms
question: What notation appears in the title of each of Psalms 120 to 134?
explanation: Each begins with “A Song of Ascents,” for example: “In my distress I cried unto the LORD, and he heard me.”

subject: Psalms
question: In Psalm 73, what helps Asaph overcome his envy of the prosperity of the wicked?
choice_b: The wise counsel of an elder
choice_c: The sudden fall of a wicked man
explanation: It stayed too painful for him “until I went into the sanctuary of God; then understood I their end.”

subject: Psalms
question: According to Psalm 1, what is the man who meditates on the law of the LORD like?
choice_a: A tree planted by streams of water
choice_b: A house built on the rock
choice_c: The chaff which the wind driveth away
choice_d: A spring that never runs dry
answer_text: A tree planted by streams of water
explanation: “He shall be like a tree planted by the rivers of water, that bringeth forth his fruit in his season”; the chaff stands for the wicked.

subject: Proverbs
question: What exhortation do we read in Proverbs 3:5?
choice_b: “Be not wise in thine own eyes”
choice_d: “Trust in the LORD with all thine heart”
answer_text: “Trust in the LORD with all thine heart”
explanation: Verse 5 calls for complete trust: “Trust in the LORD with all thine heart; and lean not unto thine own understanding.”

subject: Proverbs
question: According to Proverbs 16:18, what goes before a fall?
explanation: “Pride goeth before destruction, and an haughty spirit before a fall”: pride is the warning sign of a fall.

subject: Proverbs
question: What does Agur ask of God in his prayer?
choice_b: “Give me a wise and understanding heart”
choice_c: “Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation”
choice_d: “Make me know the name of thy son”
explanation: Agur asks: “Give me neither poverty nor riches; feed me with food convenient for me,” lest he deny God when full or steal when poor.

subject: Proverbs
question: According to Proverbs 1:7, what is “the beginning of knowledge”?
explanation: The verse says it plainly: “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge,” while fools despise wisdom and instruction.

subject: Ecclesiastes
question: What is the final conclusion of the book?
choice_b: “There is no new thing under the sun”
explanation: “Let us hear the conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God, and keep his commandments: for this is the whole duty of man.”

subject: Ecclesiastes
question: According to 5:10, what does the Preacher say about the one who loves money?
choice_b: He enjoys it to the full
explanation: “He that loveth silver shall not be satisfied with silver… this is also vanity.” Sweet sleep belongs to the laboring man.

subject: Ecclesiastes
question: According to the Preacher, what becomes of a person’s spirit when the dust returns to the earth?
choice_a: It goes down into the earth
choice_b: It wanders forever under the sun
choice_c: It dies out like that of the beast
choice_d: It returns to God who gave it
answer_text: It returns to God who gave it
explanation: The poem ends with the time when “shall the dust return to the earth as it was: and the spirit shall return unto God who gave it.”

subject: Ecclesiastes
question: How is the Preacher introduced in the first verse?
choice_a: Son of Jesse, shepherd of Bethlehem
choice_b: Son of David, king in Jerusalem
choice_c: Son of Amoz, prophet of Judah
answer_text: Son of David, king in Jerusalem
explanation: “The words of the Preacher, the son of David, king in Jerusalem.” The other titles point to David, Isaiah and Jeremiah.

subject: Song of Songs
question: According to 8:7, what can “many waters” not quench?
explanation: “Many waters cannot quench love, neither can the floods drown it.”

subject: Song of Songs
question: By what name is the beloved called in 6:13?
explanation: “Return, return, O Shulamite; return, return, that we may look upon thee.” The Shunammite is Abishag, in David’s day (1 Kgs 1:3).

subject: Song of Songs
question: To what does the bridegroom compare the Shulamite’s eyes in 7:4?
explanation: “Thine eyes are like the pools in Heshbon, by the gate of Bath-rabbim; thy nose is as the tower of Lebanon.”

subject: Song of Songs
question: Which refrain does the beloved address several times to the daughters of Jerusalem?
choice_c: “Do not stir up or awaken love”
answer_text: “Do not stir up or awaken love”
explanation: “I charge you, O daughters of Jerusalem… that you not stir up or awaken love until it pleases.” The refrain returns in 3:5 and 8:4.

subject: Isaiah
question: What name will the virgin give to the son announced to Ahaz as a sign?
explanation: “Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel.” Shear-jashub is Isaiah’s own son (7:3).

subject: Isaiah
question: What sign did God give Hezekiah to confirm that he would live fifteen more years?
choice_a: A fleece was wet with dew
choice_c: The shadow went back ten degrees
choice_d: The sun stood still a whole day
answer_text: The shadow went back ten degrees
explanation: “Behold, I will bring again the shadow of the degrees, which is gone down in the sun dial of Ahaz, ten degrees backward. So the sun returned ten degrees.”

subject: Isaiah
question: Which of these titles is not among the names of the child announced in 9:6?
explanation: “His name shall be called Wonderful, Counsellor, The mighty God, The everlasting Father, The Prince of Peace.” “King of kings” is not in this list.

subject: Isaiah
question: How many Assyrian soldiers did the angel of the LORD strike down in Sennacherib’s camp?
explanation: “Then the angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand.”

subject: Jeremiah
question: Who wrote down Jeremiah’s words at his dictation?
explanation: Jeremiah called Baruch son of Neriah, who “wrote from the mouth of Jeremiah all the words of the LORD.”

subject: Jeremiah
question: Which king cut up the scroll of the prophecies with a penknife and threw it into the fire?
explanation: The king cut the scroll with the scribe’s penknife and cast it into the fire; God then ordered it rewritten, “all the former words… which Jehoiakim the king of Judah hath burned.”

subject: Jeremiah
question: In the vision of the two baskets of figs, who represents the good figs?
explanation: God will look favorably on “them that are carried away captive of Judah” whom he sent to the land of the Chaldeans; Zedekiah, the remnant of Jerusalem and those in Egypt are the bad figs.

subject: Jeremiah
question: According to the promise of the new covenant, where will God write his law?
explanation: “I will put my law in their inward parts, and write it in their hearts”: the law will no longer be merely external, engraved on stone.

subject: Lamentations
question: When are the LORD’s compassions renewed?
explanation: “His compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.”

subject: Lamentations
question: What does the believer’s soul declare in the midst of the ruins, in chapter 3?
explanation: “The LORD is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.”

subject: Lamentations
question: Complete: “It is good for a man that he bear the … in his youth.”
explanation: “It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth”: a trial accepted early trains us in patient hope.

subject: Lamentations
question: What plea do the people address to the LORD near the end of the book?
explanation: “Turn thou us unto thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old.”

subject: Ezekiel
question: What name will the city bear at the very end of the book?
explanation: “And the name of the city from that day shall be, The LORD is there.” The book ends with God’s presence in the midst of his people.

subject: Ezekiel
question: According to chapter 18, who will bear the penalty for sin?
explanation: “The soul that sinneth, it shall die. The son shall not bear the iniquity of the father, neither shall the father bear the iniquity of the son.”

subject: Ezekiel
question: For how many days did Ezekiel have to lie on his left side for the iniquity of Israel?
explanation: Three hundred and ninety days for Israel, then forty days on his right side for Judah: “I have appointed thee each day for a year.”

subject: Ezekiel
question: What does Ezekiel see in the valley where the Spirit sets him down in chapter 37?
explanation: The LORD sets him down “in the midst of the valley which was full of bones”; there were very many in the open valley, and they were very dry.

subject: Daniel
question: What did Daniel and his companions ask to eat during the ten-day test?
choice_c: The king’s food without the wine
explanation: “Prove thy servants, I beseech thee, ten days; and let them give us vegetables to eat, and water to drink.”

subject: Daniel
question: In the vision of chapter 7, who receives dominion, glory and a kingdom from the Ancient of days?
choice_d: One like the Son of man
answer_text: One like the Son of man
explanation: “One like the Son of man came with the clouds of heaven… And there was given him dominion, and glory, and a kingdom.”

subject: Daniel
question: According to the prophecy of the seventy weeks, what will happen “after threescore and two weeks”?
explanation: “And after threescore and two weeks shall Messiah be cut off, but not for himself.”

subject: Daniel
question: Why was Daniel thrown into the lions’ den?
choice_a: He had refused to worship the statue
choice_b: He had foretold the fall of Babylon
choice_c: He kept praying despite the decree
choice_d: He had refused the king’s gifts
answer_text: He kept praying despite the decree
explanation: Knowing that the decree was signed, Daniel “kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.”

subject: Hosea
question: What was the name of the woman Hosea married at the LORD’s command?
explanation: “So he went and took Gomer the daughter of Diblaim.” Diblaim is Gomer’s father, not his wife.

subject: Hosea
question: Which valley does God promise to turn into “a door of hope”?
explanation: “I will give her her vineyards from thence, and the valley of Achor for a door of hope”: the place of Achan’s disaster becomes a place of hope.

subject: Hosea
question: The name of the first son, Jezreel, announced the punishment of which house?
explanation: “Call his name Jezreel; for yet a little while, and I will avenge the blood of Jezreel upon the house of Jehu.”

subject: Hosea
question: What does the name “Lo-Ammi,” given to the third child, mean?
explanation: The LORD explains the name: “Call his name Lo-ammi: for ye are not my people, and I will not be your God.” “No more pity” corresponds to Lo-Ruhamah.

subject: Joel
question: In which valley will God gather the nations to judge them?
explanation: “I will also gather all nations, and will bring them down into the valley of Jehoshaphat, and will plead with them there.”

subject: Joel
question: What does the LORD promise in Joel 2:25, after the locust invasion?
explanation: “I will restore to you the years that the locust hath eaten, the cankerworm, and the caterpillar, and the palmerworm, my great army.”

subject: Joel
question: To whom did Tyre, Sidon and the Philistines sell the children of Judah?
explanation: They sold the children of Judah and Jerusalem to the sons of Javan, the Greeks, “that ye might remove them far from their border.”

subject: Joel
question: Complete: “Rend your heart, and not…”
explanation: “Rend your heart, and not your garments, and turn unto the LORD your God”: God wants inward repentance, not just outward signs of mourning.

subject: Amos
question: Which priest of Bethel orders Amos to flee to Judah?
explanation: Amaziah, priest of Bethel, denounces Amos to Jeroboam and then tells him: “O thou seer, go, flee thee away into the land of Judah.”

subject: Amos
question: Which vision tells Amos that “the end is come” upon Israel?
choice_a: A wall and a plumb line
choice_b: A fire that devours the deep
explanation: “Amos, what seest thou? And I said, A basket of summer fruit. Then said the LORD unto me, The end is come upon my people of Israel.”

subject: Amos
question: Who quotes Amos 9:11-12 at the council of Jerusalem to show that the nations are welcomed?
explanation: James speaks up and cites the prophets: “I will build again the tabernacle of David, which is fallen down … and all the Gentiles, upon whom my name is called.”

subject: Amos
question: Complete: “Let justice run down as waters, and righteousness as…”
choice_b: a mighty stream that never dries up
choice_d: the abundant dew of the morning
answer_text: a mighty stream that never dries up
explanation: “But let judgment run down as waters, and righteousness as a mighty stream”: God wants justice rather than feasts.

subject: Obadiah
question: Against which people is the whole prophecy of Obadiah directed?
explanation: “Thus saith the Lord GOD concerning Edom… Arise ye, and let us rise up against her in battle.”

subject: Obadiah
question: Which rule sums up the day of the LORD for the nations, according to Obadiah?
choice_a: “An eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth”
choice_b: “The just shall live by his faith”
choice_c: “Be strong and of a good courage”
choice_d: “As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee”
answer_text: “As thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee”
explanation: “For the day of the LORD is near upon all the heathen: as thou hast done, it shall be done unto thee: thy reward shall return upon thine own head.”

subject: Obadiah
question: Where are the “captives of Jerusalem” who will possess the cities of the south?
explanation: “The captivity of Jerusalem, which is in Sepharad, shall possess the cities of the south”; Zarephath marks the limit of the land retaken by the captives of Israel.

subject: Obadiah
question: From which patriarch does Edom descend?
explanation: “Esau is Edom… these are the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites”; Obadiah, in fact, speaks of “the mount of Esau.” Moab and Ammon descend from Lot.

subject: Jonah
question: How long does Jonah stay in the belly of the fish?
explanation: “Jonah was in the belly of the fish three days and three nights,” a sign that Jesus would take up for himself.

subject: Jonah
question: What does the king of Nineveh do when the message reaches him?
choice_a: He has Jonah thrown into prison
choice_b: He offers sacrifices to his gods
choice_d: He flees out of the city
explanation: “He arose from his throne, and he laid his robe from him, and covered him with sackcloth, and sat in ashes.”

subject: Jonah
question: Why had Jonah fled to Tarshish, according to what he admits himself?
choice_a: He feared being killed in Nineveh
choice_b: He did not know how to speak well
choice_c: He wanted to preach to Israel
choice_d: He knew God to be compassionate
answer_text: He knew God to be compassionate
explanation: “Therefore I fled before unto Tarshish: for I knew that thou art a gracious God, and merciful, slow to anger, and of great kindness, and repentest thee of the evil.”

subject: Jonah
question: What plant does God make grow to shade Jonah?
explanation: “The LORD God prepared a gourd, and made it to come up over Jonah, that it might be a shadow over his head.”

subject: Micah
question: Where, according to Micah, will God cast the sins of his people?
choice_c: As far as the east is from the west
choice_d: Into the depths of the sea
answer_text: Into the depths of the sea
explanation: “He will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.”

subject: Micah
question: In the Gospel, who quotes Micah’s prophecy about Bethlehem to King Herod?
choice_c: The shepherds from the nearby fields
explanation: Herod gathered all the chief priests and scribes of the people together; they answered him: “In Bethlehem of Judea: for thus it is written by the prophet.”

subject: Micah
question: With what question does the closing praise of the book of Micah begin?
choice_c: “Who knoweth if he will not return?”
choice_d: “Who is a God like unto thee?”
answer_text: “Who is a God like unto thee?”
explanation: “Who is a God like unto thee, that pardoneth iniquity…?” “Where is the LORD thy God?” is, by contrast, the taunt of the enemy.

subject: Micah
question: Complete Micah 6:8: “…to love mercy, and to walk … with thy God.”
explanation: “What doth the LORD require of thee, but to do justly, and to love mercy, and to walk humbly with thy God?”

subject: Nahum
question: What does Nahum call Nineveh at the start of his last oracle?
explanation: “Woe to the bloody city! it is all full of lies and robbery; the prey departeth not.”

subject: Nahum
question: To which Egyptian city, already fallen, is Nineveh compared?
explanation: “Art thou better than populous No, that was situate among the rivers?… Yet was she carried away, she went into captivity.”

subject: Nahum
question: How does the book of Nahum end?
choice_a: With a prayer of the prophet Nahum
choice_b: With a victory song of Judah
choice_c: With a question to the king of Assyria
choice_d: With a promise of pardon for Nineveh
answer_text: With a question to the king of Assyria
explanation: The book closes by addressing the king of Assyria: “for upon whom hath not thy wickedness passed continually?”

subject: Nahum
question: Which city is at the center of Nahum’s whole prophecy?
explanation: The book opens with these words: “The burden of Nineveh. The book of the vision of Nahum the Elkoshite.”

subject: Habakkuk
question: With what question does Habakkuk open his dialogue with God?
choice_b: “O LORD, how long shall I cry?”
answer_text: “O LORD, how long shall I cry?”
explanation: “O LORD, how long shall I cry, and thou wilt not hear! even cry out unto thee of violence, and thou wilt not save!”

subject: Habakkuk
question: Where does Habakkuk stand to wait for God’s answer?
explanation: “I will stand upon my watch, and set me upon the tower, and will watch to see what he will say unto me.”

subject: Habakkuk
question: From where does God come, according to Habakkuk’s prayer?
explanation: “God came from Teman, and the Holy One from mount Paran… His glory covered the heavens, and the earth was full of his praise.”

subject: Habakkuk
question: Which people does God announce he will raise up to punish Judah?
explanation: “Lo, I raise up the Chaldeans, that bitter and hasty nation, which shall march through the breadth of the land.”

subject: Zephaniah
question: Under which king of Judah does Zephaniah prophesy?
explanation: The word came to Zephaniah “in the days of Josiah the son of Amon, king of Judah.” Hezekiah appears only in his genealogy.

subject: Zephaniah
question: What will God give the peoples so that they all call on his name?
explanation: “Then will I give the peoples pure lips, that they may all call upon the name of the LORD, to serve him with one consent.”

subject: Zephaniah
question: What proud motto does the “rejoicing city” of Nineveh say in her heart?
choice_a: “I am, and there is none beside me”
choice_c: “I shall be a queen for ever”
answer_text: “I am, and there is none beside me”
explanation: “This is the rejoicing city that dwelt carelessly, that said in her heart, I am, and there is none beside me.”

subject: Zephaniah
question: Which city of Assyria will become a desolation according to Zephaniah?
explanation: “He will destroy Assyria; and will make Nineveh a desolation, and dry like a wilderness.”

subject: Haggai
question: Who are the two leaders Haggai addresses?
explanation: The word comes “unto Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua the son of Jehozadak, the high priest.”

subject: Haggai
question: What lesson does Haggai draw from his questions to the priests about consecrated meat and the corpse?
choice_a: Sacrifices are enough to purify the people
choice_b: Only the Levites may touch holy meat
choice_c: Uncleanness is transmitted by contact, holiness is not
choice_d: The temple purifies everything that enters it
answer_text: Uncleanness is transmitted by contact, holiness is not
explanation: Consecrated flesh does not make holy what it touches, but contact with a corpse defiles: “that which they offer there is unclean.”

subject: Haggai
question: During which feast does Haggai’s second message, on the twenty-first day of the seventh month, fall?
explanation: “The fifteenth day of this seventh month shall be the feast of tabernacles for seven days”: the twenty-first is its last day.

subject: Haggai
question: What excuse did the people give for not rebuilding the temple?
choice_a: We do not have enough money
choice_c: The king has not permitted it
explanation: “This people say, The time is not come, the time that the LORD’s house should be built.”

subject: Zechariah
question: On which mountain will the LORD’s feet stand on the day of the LORD?
explanation: “His feet shall stand in that day upon the mount of Olives, which is before Jerusalem on the east”; it will split in the middle.

subject: Zechariah
question: In the vision of Joshua the high priest, who stands at his right hand to accuse him?
explanation: Joshua was standing before the angel of the LORD, “and Satan standing at his right hand” to accuse him; the LORD rebukes him.

subject: Zechariah
question: Which month is named for the visions Zechariah receives during the night?
explanation: “Upon the four and twentieth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat… I saw by night.” Kislev is the month of the message in chapter 7.

subject: Zechariah
question: According to Zechariah 9:9, on what animal does the king of Zion make his entry?
explanation: “Behold, thy King cometh unto thee: he is just, and having salvation; lowly, and riding upon an ass, and upon a colt the foal of an ass.”

subject: Malachi
question: What kind of animals did the priests lay on the altar?
explanation: “If ye offer the blind for sacrifice, is it not evil? and if ye offer the lame and sick, is it not evil?”

subject: Malachi
question: What is written before God for those who fear him and honor his name?
explanation: “The LORD hearkened, and heard it, and a book of remembrance was written before him for them that feared the LORD.”

subject: Malachi
question: With whom had God made “a covenant of life and peace,” betrayed by the priests?
explanation: “That my covenant might be with Levi, saith the LORD of hosts. My covenant was with him of life and peace.”

subject: Malachi
question: Which prophet does God promise to send before the great and dreadful day of the LORD?
explanation: “Behold, I will send you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and dreadful day of the LORD.”

subject: Matthew
question: What gifts do the magi offer the young child?
explanation: Having opened their treasures, the magi “presented unto him gifts; gold, and frankincense, and myrrh.”

subject: Matthew
question: How many generations does Matthew count in each of the three sets of the genealogy?
explanation: “Fourteen generations” from Abraham to David, fourteen from David until the carrying away into Babylon, and fourteen from then unto Christ.

subject: Matthew
question: According to Matthew 28, what do the chief priests pay the soldiers to say?
choice_a: That the disciples stole the body
choice_b: That Jesus had not really died
choice_c: That an angel carried the body away
choice_d: That the women went to the wrong tomb
answer_text: That the disciples stole the body
explanation: They give the soldiers large money, saying: “Say ye, His disciples came by night, and stole him away while we slept.”

subject: Matthew
question: On what does the wise man in the Sermon on the Mount build his house?
explanation: Whoever hears these sayings and does them is “a wise man, which built his house upon a rock.”

subject: Mark
question: What name does the unclean spirit in the country of the Gadarenes give?
explanation: Asked by Jesus, he answers: “My name is Legion: for we are many.”

subject: Mark
question: According to Jesus, why did the Son of man come?
choice_a: To be served by his own
choice_b: To serve and to give his life
choice_d: To abolish the law of Moses
answer_text: To serve and to give his life
explanation: “For even the Son of man came not to be ministered unto, but to minister, and to give his life a ransom for many.”

subject: Mark
question: Which blind man does Jesus heal in two stages, the man first seeing people “as trees”?
explanation: At Bethsaida, the blind man first sees men “as trees, walking,” then sees everything clearly after a second laying on of hands.

subject: Mark
question: How much does the poor widow put into the temple treasury?
explanation: “She threw in two mites, which make a farthing”: all that she had, even all her living.

subject: Luke
question: Which tree does Zacchaeus climb to see Jesus?
explanation: Being short, Zacchaeus “ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree to see him.”

subject: Luke
question: Why does Zechariah become mute?
choice_a: Because he made a vow of silence
choice_b: Because he did not believe the angel
choice_d: Because he saw the glory of God
answer_text: Because he did not believe the angel
explanation: Gabriel tells him: “thou shalt be dumb… because thou believest not my words, which shall be fulfilled in their season.”

subject: Luke
question: To whom does Pilate send Jesus after learning that he belonged to that ruler’s jurisdiction?
explanation: Learning that Jesus “belonged unto Herod’s jurisdiction,” Pilate sent him to Herod, who was himself at Jerusalem at that time.

subject: Luke
question: To whom does Luke dedicate his Gospel?
explanation: Luke writes that it seemed good to him to set everything down “in order, most excellent Theophilus.”

subject: John
question: What does Thomas confess when he sees the risen Jesus?
explanation: Invited to touch the nail marks, “Thomas answered and said unto him, My Lord and my God.”

subject: John
question: According to John, what is Jesus’ last word before he gives up his spirit?
explanation: “When Jesus therefore had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished: and he bowed his head, and gave up the ghost.”

subject: John
question: According to the conclusion of John 20, why were these things written?
choice_a: To keep the facts in order
choice_d: So that people may believe and have life
answer_text: So that people may believe and have life
explanation: “These are written, that ye might believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God; and that believing ye might have life through his name.”

subject: John
question: Which Pharisee comes to Jesus by night and learns that one must be born again?
explanation: “There was a man of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews: the same came to Jesus by night”; Jesus tells him he must be born again.

subject: Acts
question: In which city are the disciples first called “Christians”?
explanation: Barnabas and Saul taught there a whole year, and “the disciples were called Christians first in Antioch.”

subject: Acts
question: What is the Ethiopian eunuch reading in his chariot when Philip joins him?
explanation: He is reading the passage of Isaiah: “He was led as a sheep to the slaughter,” and Philip preaches Jesus to him, beginning at that Scripture.

subject: Acts
question: At the end of the first journey, through which cities do Paul and Barnabas pass back, in order, after Derbe?
explanation: After evangelizing Derbe, “they returned again to Lystra, and to Iconium, and Antioch,” confirming the souls of the disciples.

subject: Acts
question: About how many people are added to the disciples on the day of Pentecost?
explanation: Those who gladly received Peter’s word were baptized: “the same day there were added unto them about three thousand souls.” The figure of five thousand men comes only later.

subject: Romans
question: According to 8:1, what is there “now” no more of for those who are in Christ Jesus?
explanation: “There is therefore now no condemnation to them which are in Christ Jesus”: this is the opening of chapter 8.

subject: Romans
question: In chapter 11, to what tree does Paul compare Israel, onto which the Gentiles have been grafted?
explanation: The Gentile is “a wild olive tree” grafted in among the branches that were broken off; he must not boast, for “thou bearest not the root, but the root thee.”

subject: Romans
question: Complete the parallel between Adam and Christ: “as by one man’s disobedience many were made sinners, so by the … of one shall many be made righteous”
explanation: Adam’s disobedience is answered by Christ’s obedience: one man brings condemnation, one man brings righteousness.

subject: Romans
question: According to Paul, what is “the wages of sin”?
explanation: “For the wages of sin is death; but the gift of God is eternal life through Jesus Christ our Lord.”

subject: 1 Corinthians
question: Of what is the believer’s body the temple, according to Paul?
explanation: “Your body is the temple of the Holy Ghost which is in you… and ye are not your own”: hence the call to flee sexual immorality.

subject: 1 Corinthians
question: Which sin, tolerated by the church, does Paul denounce in chapter 5?
choice_a: A man was living with his father’s wife
choice_b: An elder was embezzling the collection
choice_d: A brother had denied Christ in public
answer_text: A man was living with his father’s wife
explanation: “That one should have his father’s wife”: a sexual immorality “not so much as named among the Gentiles,” and the church was puffed up about it.

subject: 1 Corinthians
question: In chapter 8, what will Paul do if food makes his brother stumble?
choice_a: He will rebuke him in public
choice_b: He will eat apart from him
choice_c: He will never eat meat again
choice_d: He will urge him to be stronger
answer_text: He will never eat meat again
explanation: Even though an idol is nothing, Paul gives up his freedom: “if meat make my brother to offend, I will eat no flesh while the world standeth.”

subject: 1 Corinthians
question: From whom did Paul learn that there were quarrels in the church at Corinth?
explanation: “It hath been declared unto me of you, my brethren, by them which are of the house of Chloe, that there are contentions among you”: some claim Paul, others Apollos or Cephas.

subject: 2 Corinthians
question: What answer does the Lord give Paul when he asks him to take away his thorn?
explanation: “My grace is sufficient for thee: for my strength is made perfect in weakness.” So Paul will boast all the more gladly of his weaknesses.

subject: 2 Corinthians
question: Which churches does Paul cite as an example of generosity despite their deep poverty?
explanation: In the churches of Macedonia, “their deep poverty abounded unto the riches of their liberality,” beyond their means.

subject: 2 Corinthians
question: What difference does Paul draw between godly sorrow and the sorrow of the world?
choice_a: The first is fleeting, the second lasts forever
choice_b: The first leads to salvation, the second to death
choice_c: The first comes from the Spirit, the second from the law
choice_d: The first is lived in secret, the second in public
answer_text: The first leads to salvation, the second to death
explanation: “Godly sorrow worketh repentance to salvation not to be repented of: but the sorrow of the world worketh death.”

subject: 2 Corinthians
question: Complete: “If any man be in Christ, he is…”
explanation: “He is a new creature: old things are passed away; behold, all things are become new.”

subject: Galatians
question: What is Paul’s reaction at the start of the letter, in place of the usual thanksgiving?
choice_a: He thanks God for their faith
choice_b: He is astonished at how quickly they are turning away
answer_text: He is astonished at how quickly they are turning away
explanation: “I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you… unto another gospel.”

subject: Galatians
question: Where did Paul go right after his conversion, instead of going up to Jerusalem to consult the apostles?
explanation: “Neither went I up to Jerusalem to them which were apostles before me; but I went into Arabia, and returned again unto Damascus.”

subject: Galatians
question: How many years after the promise made to Abraham did the law come, according to Paul?
explanation: The law, “which was four hundred and thirty years after,” cannot annul a covenant that God had confirmed earlier.

subject: Galatians
question: Which of these does Paul include in the fruit of the Spirit?
explanation: “The fruit of the Spirit is love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, temperance.”

subject: Ephesians
question: How are husbands to love their wives?
choice_d: As one loves a brother in the faith
explanation: “Husbands, love your wives, even as Christ also loved the church, and gave himself for it.”

subject: Ephesians
question: Why did Christ give apostles, prophets, evangelists, pastors and teachers?
choice_a: To govern in place of the elders
choice_b: For the perfecting of the saints
choice_c: To carry out the entire ministry by themselves
choice_d: To replace the reading of Scripture
answer_text: For the perfecting of the saints
explanation: These gifts are “for the perfecting of the saints, for the work of the ministry, for the edifying of the body of Christ.”

subject: Ephesians
question: Against whom must the believer wrestle, according to chapter 6?
choice_a: Against the wicked spirits in the heavenly places
choice_b: Against the magistrates who persecute the church
choice_c: Against the Jewish teachers who demand circumcision
choice_d: Against the unbelieving members of his family
answer_text: Against the wicked spirits in the heavenly places
explanation: “We wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places” (literally, in the heavenly places).

subject: Ephesians
question: What must not go down upon your wrath?
explanation: “Be ye angry, and sin not: let not the sun go down upon your wrath: neither give place to the devil.”

subject: Philippians
question: What has Paul learned, he who can do all things “through Christ which strengtheneth me”?
choice_b: To refuse every gift from the churches
choice_c: To be content in every situation
choice_d: To hide his needs from his brothers
answer_text: To be content in every situation
explanation: “I have learned, in whatsoever state I am, therewith to be content… both to be full and to be hungry, both to abound and to suffer need. I can do all things through Christ which strengtheneth me.”

subject: Philippians
question: According to chapter 1, what effect did Paul’s captivity have?
choice_a: It scattered the church at Rome
choice_c: It reduced the preachers to silence
choice_d: It forced Paul to stop writing
explanation: “The things which happened unto me have fallen out rather unto the furtherance of the gospel”: his bonds are manifest in all the palace, and the brethren speak the word with more boldness.

subject: Philippians
question: What did the Philippians do for Paul when he was in Thessalonica?
choice_a: They came to free him from prison
choice_b: They sent him help more than once
choice_d: They wrote him a letter of support
answer_text: They sent him help more than once
explanation: They were the only church to support him: “even in Thessalonica ye sent once and again unto my necessity.”

subject: Philippians
question: Complete the exhortation Paul repeats: “… in the Lord alway: and again I say, …”
explanation: “Rejoice in the Lord alway: and again I say, Rejoice”: joy runs through this whole letter written in chains.

subject: Colossians
question: In which neighboring church is the letter also to be read?
explanation: “Cause that it be read also in the church of the Laodiceans; and that ye likewise read the epistle from Laodicea.”

subject: Colossians
question: What “mystery” does Paul proclaim among the Gentiles?
choice_a: Christ in you, the hope of glory
choice_b: The coming destruction of the temple
choice_c: The secrets of the unseen world of angels
choice_d: The law written on tablets of stone
answer_text: Christ in you, the hope of glory
explanation: “The riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles; which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.”

subject: Colossians
question: According to Paul, what did festivals, new moons and sabbaths represent?
choice_a: Burdens laid on by the Pharisees
choice_d: A shadow of things to come
answer_text: A shadow of things to come
explanation: “Let no man therefore judge you in meat, or in drink, or in respect of an holyday, or of the new moon, or of the sabbath days: which are a shadow of things to come; but the body is of Christ.”

subject: Colossians
question: Who taught the gospel to the Colossians?
explanation: They learned it of Epaphras, “our dear fellowservant, who is for you a faithful minister of Christ.”

subject: 1 Thessalonians
question: How will the day of the Lord come, according to 5:2?
choice_a: As a thief in the night
choice_c: Like a storm in broad daylight
choice_d: Like a fire in the forest
answer_text: As a thief in the night
explanation: Paul reminds the Thessalonians that they themselves know perfectly well that “the day of the Lord so cometh as a thief in the night.”

subject: 1 Thessalonians
question: What images does Paul use in chapter 2 to describe his attitude toward the Thessalonians?
explanation: Paul was gentle “as a nurse cherisheth her children,” and he treated each one “as a father doth his children.”

subject: 1 Thessalonians
question: In which city had Paul been “shamefully entreated” just before preaching the gospel at Thessalonica?
explanation: “Even after that we had suffered before, and were shamefully entreated, as ye know, at Philippi, we were bold in our God to speak unto you the gospel of God.”

subject: 1 Thessalonians
question: Complete: “Rejoice evermore. Pray…”
explanation: The exhortations come in a row: “Rejoice evermore. Pray without ceasing. In every thing give thanks.”

subject: 2 Thessalonians
question: What rumor was troubling the Thessalonians?
choice_a: That Paul had died in prison in Corinth
choice_b: That the resurrection had already happened
choice_c: That the day of the Lord had already come
choice_d: That Gentiles could not be saved
answer_text: That the day of the Lord had already come
explanation: They were troubled by a word or a letter attributed to Paul, claiming, as it were, that “the day of the Lord had already come.” A resurrection that had already happened was the error of Hymenaeus and Philetus (2 Tim 2:18).

subject: 2 Thessalonians
question: According to 2:3, what must happen before the day of the Lord?
choice_b: The falling away and the appearance of the man of sin
choice_c: The preaching of the gospel in Rome
choice_d: The death of all the apostles
answer_text: The falling away and the appearance of the man of sin
explanation: “That day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition.”

subject: 2 Thessalonians
question: According to 1:8, the Lord will punish “them that know not God” and which other group?
choice_a: Those who love the present age
choice_c: Those who obey not the gospel
choice_d: Those who have denied the Lord
answer_text: Those who obey not the gospel
explanation: He will take vengeance “on them that know not God, and that obey not the gospel of our Lord Jesus Christ.”

subject: 2 Thessalonians
question: According to 2:8, who will destroy the wicked one?
explanation: “Then shall that Wicked be revealed, whom the Lord shall consume with the spirit of his mouth, and shall destroy with the brightness of his coming.”

subject: 1 Timothy
question: According to 2:5, how does Paul describe the one mediator between God and men?
explanation: “There is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus; who gave himself a ransom for all.”

subject: 1 Timothy
question: Why does Paul advise Timothy to drink a little wine?
explanation: “Drink no longer water, but use a little wine for thy stomach’s sake and thine often infirmities.”

subject: 1 Timothy
question: According to 4:3, what did the false teachers of the latter times prescribe?
explanation: They are “forbidding to marry, and commanding to abstain from meats, which God hath created to be received with thanksgiving.”

subject: 1 Timothy
question: According to 6:10, the love of money is…
choice_a: a root of all kinds of evil
answer_text: a root of all kinds of evil
explanation: “The love of money is a root of all kinds of evil,” and some who were eager for it “have erred from the faith.”

subject: 2 Timothy
question: Complete: “I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, …”
explanation: “I have fought a good fight, I have finished my course, I have kept the faith.” The crown of righteousness, for its part, is still laid up for him.

subject: 2 Timothy
question: What does Paul ask Timothy to bring from Troas, along with the books and the parchments?
explanation: “The cloak that I left at Troas with Carpus, when thou comest, bring with thee, and the books, but especially the parchments.”

subject: 2 Timothy
question: Where did Paul leave Trophimus sick?
explanation: “Erastus abode at Corinth: but Trophimus have I left at Miletum sick.” Troas is where the cloak had been left.

subject: 2 Timothy
question: What were the names of Timothy’s grandmother and mother?
explanation: The sincere faith in Timothy “dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice.”

subject: Titus
question: What was Titus to appoint in every city?
explanation: Paul asks him to “ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.”

subject: Titus
question: According to 2:11-12, what does the grace of God teach us?
explanation: Grace is “teaching us that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we should live soberly, righteously, and godly, in this present world.”

subject: Titus
question: Whom does Paul plan to send to Crete so that Titus can join him?
explanation: “When I shall send Artemas unto thee, or Tychicus, be diligent to come unto me to Nicopolis.”

subject: Titus
question: On which island did Paul leave Titus?
explanation: “For this cause left I thee in Crete, that thou shouldest set in order the things that are wanting.”

subject: Philemon
question: What is the name of the slave for whom Paul intercedes?
explanation: “I beseech thee for my son Onesimus, whom I have begotten in my bonds.”

subject: Philemon
question: What does Paul ask Philemon to prepare for him?
explanation: “Prepare me also a lodging: for I trust that through your prayers I shall be given unto you.”

subject: Philemon
question: Who is called “our fellowsoldier” in verse 2?
explanation: Paul writes “to our beloved Apphia, and Archippus our fellowsoldier, and to the church in thy house.”

subject: Philemon
question: Where does the church greeted at the beginning of the letter meet?
explanation: The letter is addressed “unto Philemon,” and Paul also greets “the church in thy house.”

subject: Hebrews
question: How is faith defined in Hebrews 11:1?
choice_a: Faithful obedience to the whole law
choice_b: The substance of things hoped for
choice_c: A knowledge reserved for the perfect
choice_d: A feeling of peace in the midst of trials
answer_text: The substance of things hoped for
explanation: “Now faith is the substance of things hoped for, the evidence of things not seen.”

subject: Hebrews
question: According to 4:8, which figure did not give the people the true rest?
explanation: “For if Jesus [Joshua] had given them rest, then would he not afterward have spoken of another day.”

subject: Hebrews
question: In the quotation of Psalm 40 in 10:5, what does Christ say to God: “thou hast prepared me …”?
explanation: “Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”: the perfect offering is the body of Jesus Christ.

subject: Hebrews
question: To what is hope compared in 6:19?
explanation: “Which hope we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and steadfast, and which entereth into that within the veil.”

subject: James
question: According to James, what does the trying of faith produce?
explanation: “The trying of your faith worketh patience,” and patience must have its perfect work.

subject: James
question: What does “pure religion and undefiled” consist of, according to James?
choice_a: Keeping the Sabbath and the feasts
explanation: It consists in “visit[ing] the fatherless and widows in their affliction, and to keep[ing] himself unspotted from the world.”

subject: James
question: According to James, how long did it not rain after Elijah’s prayer?
explanation: Elijah prayed earnestly, “and it rained not on the earth by the space of three years and six months.”

subject: James
question: To whom does James address his letter?
choice_b: To the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad
choice_c: To the seven churches which are in Asia
choice_d: To the saints and faithful brethren at Colosse
answer_text: To the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad
explanation: James writes “to the twelve tribes which are scattered abroad.” The “strangers scattered” are the recipients of 1 Peter.

subject: 1 Peter
question: By what were believers redeemed, according to Peter?
choice_a: By the precious blood of Christ
choice_b: By the silver and gold of the temple
answer_text: By the precious blood of Christ
explanation: Not with silver and gold, “but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot.”

subject: 1 Peter
question: What must we always be ready to give an answer about, according to 3:15?
choice_b: The hope that is in you
choice_d: The way you run your household
answer_text: The hope that is in you
explanation: “Be ready always to give an answer to every man that asketh you a reason of the hope that is in you with meekness and fear.”

subject: 1 Peter
question: Where, according to Peter, will judgment begin?
choice_b: With the kings of the earth
explanation: “The time is come that judgment must begin at the house of God: and if it first begin at us, what shall the end be of them that obey not the gospel of God?”

subject: 1 Peter
question: From where does Peter say a church greets his readers?
explanation: Peter closes: “The church that is at Babylon, elected together with you, saluteth you; and so doth Marcus my son.”

subject: 2 Peter
question: According to Peter, what has God’s divine power given us?
choice_a: Wealth, health, and a long life
choice_b: All things that pertain unto life and godliness
choice_c: Victory over all the pagan nations
choice_d: A secret knowledge reserved for the perfect
answer_text: All things that pertain unto life and godliness
explanation: “According as his divine power hath given unto us all things that pertain unto life and godliness, through the knowledge of him that hath called us.”

subject: 2 Peter
question: What is the last virtue in the list that Peter asks us to add to faith?
explanation: The list culminates thus: “to godliness brotherly kindness; and to brotherly kindness charity,” that is, love.

subject: 2 Peter
question: According to 2:16, by what was Balaam rebuked for his transgression?
choice_c: By a dream in the night
explanation: Balaam was rebuked for his iniquity: “the dumb ass speaking with man’s voice forbad the madness of the prophet.”

subject: 2 Peter
question: Which apostle does Peter call “our beloved brother”?
explanation: “Even as our beloved brother Paul also according to the wisdom given unto him hath written unto you.”

subject: 1 John
question: What “message” does John declare at the beginning of his letter (1:5)?
explanation: “This then is the message which we have heard of him, and declare unto you, that God is light, and in him is no darkness at all.”

subject: 1 John
question: Which figure does John give as a counter-example of brotherly love?
explanation: We are to love one another, “not as Cain, who was of that wicked one, and slew his brother.”

subject: 1 John
question: Which three groups does John address in turn in 2:12-14?
choice_a: Little children, fathers, and young men
choice_b: The elders, the older women, and the young men
answer_text: Little children, fathers, and young men
explanation: John writes in turn: “I write unto you, little children,” “I write unto you, fathers,” “I write unto you, young men.”

subject: 1 John
question: Which statement about God does John repeat twice in chapter 4?
explanation: “He that loveth not knoweth not God; for God is love”; and further on: “God is love; and he that dwelleth in love dwelleth in God.”

subject: 2 John
question: How does the author of 2 John introduce himself?
explanation: The letter opens with “The elder unto the elect lady and her children.” The author gives neither a personal name nor the title of apostle.

subject: 2 John
question: What should be done if someone comes without bringing the doctrine of Christ?
choice_a: Rebuke him in front of the whole church
choice_b: Not receive him into your house
choice_c: Warn him twice, then avoid him
choice_d: Welcome him in order to teach him better
answer_text: Not receive him into your house
explanation: “If there come any unto you, and bring not this doctrine, receive him not into your house, neither bid him God speed.”

subject: 2 John
question: Why does the elder say “Look to yourselves”?
choice_a: So that you do not fall into temptation
choice_b: So that you do not lose the fruit of your labor
choice_c: So that you are not handed over to the courts
choice_d: So that you do not fall from grace
answer_text: So that you do not lose the fruit of your labor
explanation: “Look to yourselves, that we lose not those things which we have wrought, but that we receive a full reward.”

subject: 2 John
question: What commandment “from the beginning” does the elder recall?
choice_a: That we honor our father and mother
choice_b: That we keep the Sabbath day
explanation: “Not as though I wrote a new commandment unto thee, but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another.”

subject: 3 John
question: What is the elder’s greatest joy?
choice_a: That the churches are growing in number
choice_b: That his children walk in truth
choice_c: That the Gentiles receive the word of God
choice_d: That the brothers live in unity
answer_text: That his children walk in truth
explanation: “I have no greater joy than to hear that my children walk in truth.”

subject: 3 John
question: What does Diotrephes do to those who would receive the brothers?
choice_a: He hands them over to the magistrates
choice_b: He drives them out of the church
choice_d: He accuses them before the elder
answer_text: He drives them out of the church
explanation: Diotrephes does not receive the brothers, “and forbiddeth them that would, and casteth them out of the church.”

subject: 3 John
question: What are believers called in the closing greeting?
explanation: “Our friends salute thee. Greet the friends by name.” Neither “saints” nor “brothers” appears in this greeting.

subject: 3 John
question: Which man does the elder criticize because he “loveth to be first”?
explanation: “Diotrephes, who loveth to be first among them, receiveth us not.” Demas, Alexander, and Hymenaeus are named critically by Paul, not by the elder.

subject: Jude
question: Whose brother does Jude say he is?
explanation: “Jude, the servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James.” He calls himself a servant, without claiming the title of apostle.

subject: Jude
question: Which three Old Testament figures does Jude associate with the ungodly?
explanation: “They have gone in the way of Cain, and ran greedily after the error of Balaam for reward, and perished in the gainsaying of Core [Korah].”

subject: Jude
question: For some, Jude asks for mercy mixed with fear. What are we to hate?
explanation: “Others save with fear, pulling them out of the fire; hating even the garment spotted by the flesh.”

subject: Jude
question: About what did the archangel Michael contend with the devil?
explanation: “Michael the archangel, when contending with the devil he disputed about the body of Moses, durst not bring against him a railing accusation.”

subject: Revelation
question: Which church does Christ rebuke because it is “neither cold nor hot”?
explanation: To the angel of the church of Laodicea: “Because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I will spit thee out of my mouth.”

subject: Revelation
question: Which church “left its first love”?
explanation: To the angel of the church in Ephesus, Christ says: “I have somewhat against thee, because thou hast left thy first love.”

subject: Revelation
question: Which names are written on the twelve gates of the New Jerusalem?
choice_a: Those of the twelve apostles of the Lamb
choice_b: Those of the seven churches of Asia
choice_d: Those of the twelve tribes of Israel
answer_text: Those of the twelve tribes of Israel
explanation: The gates bear “the names of the twelve tribes of the children of Israel”; the names of the twelve apostles are on the foundations of the wall.

subject: Revelation
question: On which island was John when he received the revelation?
explanation: “I John … was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

subject: Aaron
question: What service did God consecrate Aaron and his sons to?
explanation: God told Moses to take Aaron and his sons “that he may minister unto me in the priest’s office.”

subject: Aaron
question: What were the names of Aaron’s two sons who were consumed for offering strange fire?
explanation: Nadab and Abihu offered “strange fire before the LORD,” and fire went out from the LORD and devoured them. Eleazar and Ithamar survived.

subject: Abigail
question: Who married Abigail after her husband’s death?
explanation: David heard that Nabal was dead and sent word asking Abigail to be his wife; she went with his messengers and “became his wife.”

subject: Abigail
question: Abigail says Nabal is “as his name is.” What does she say is with him?
explanation: “Nabal is his name, and folly is with him.” The narrator had called him “churlish and evil in his doings”; Abigail goes straight to his folly.

subject: Abraham
question: How old was Abram when he left Haran?
explanation: “Abram was seventy and five years old when he departed out of Haran.” He would be 86 at Ishmael’s birth and 100 at Isaac’s.

subject: Abraham
question: To whom did Abram give a tithe of everything when he returned from his victory over the kings?
explanation: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of the most high God, blessed Abram, “and he gave him tithes of all.” From the king of Sodom, Abram refused to take anything.

subject: Absalom
question: What was the name of Absalom’s sister, who was violated by Amnon?
explanation: “Absalom the son of David had a fair sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.” Maacah was their mother.

subject: Absalom
question: What did Absalom do to make Joab, who refused to come, visit him?
choice_a: He set Joab’s field on fire
answer_text: He set Joab’s field on fire
explanation: Absalom told his servants, “Joab’s field is near mine, and he hath barley there; go and set it on fire.” Joab came at once.

subject: Ahab
question: Who was Ahab’s father?
explanation: “So Omri slept with his fathers… and Ahab his son reigned in his stead.” Jeroboam and Baasha were other kings of Israel; Ethbaal was Jezebel’s father.

subject: Ahab
question: How did Ahab react to Elijah’s words about the fate of his house?
choice_a: He tore his clothes and fasted
choice_b: He sent for Elijah to kill him
choice_c: He offered a sacrifice to Baal
choice_d: He consulted his four hundred prophets
answer_text: He tore his clothes and fasted
explanation: He “rent his clothes, and put sackcloth upon his flesh, and fasted.” Because he humbled himself, God postponed the disaster until after his death.

subject: Adam and Eve
question: Why did Adam name his wife Eve?
choice_a: Because she was formed from the man’s rib
choice_b: Because she was the mother of all living
choice_c: Because she was deceived by the serpent
choice_d: Because she was the first to eat the fruit
answer_text: Because she was the mother of all living
explanation: “Adam called his wife’s name Eve; because she was the mother of all living.” “Taken out of man” explains the word “woman” instead.

subject: Adam and Eve
question: Complete Adam’s answer to God: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me…”
explanation: “The woman whom thou gavest to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I did eat”: Adam shifts the blame to his wife. It is Eve who will say, “The serpent beguiled me.”

subject: Hagar and Ishmael
question: What country was Hagar from?
explanation: Sarai “had an handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.” Later, Hagar would also take an Egyptian wife for her son Ishmael.

subject: Hagar and Ishmael
question: Where did the angel of the LORD find Hagar as she was fleeing?
choice_a: By a spring on the way to Shur
answer_text: By a spring on the way to Shur
explanation: The angel “found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.” Beersheba is the wilderness where she would wander later.

subject: Amos
question: During the reign of which king of Israel did Amos receive his visions?
explanation: His visions date “in the days of Uzziah king of Judah, and in the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash king of Israel.”

subject: Amos
question: How does Amos answer Amaziah, who forbids him to prophesy at Bethel?
choice_a: He was trained at a school of prophets
choice_b: He is the servant of the king of Judah
choice_c: He is the son of a priest of Bethel
choice_d: He is neither a prophet nor a prophet’s son
answer_text: He is neither a prophet nor a prophet’s son
explanation: Amos answers, “I was no prophet, neither was I a prophet’s son; but I was an herdman, and a gatherer of sycomore fruit.”

subject: Ananias of Damascus
question: What did Ananias call Saul as he laid his hands on him?
explanation: Ananias said, “Brother Saul, the Lord, even Jesus… hath sent me, that thou mightest receive thy sight, and be filled with the Holy Spirit.”

subject: Ananias of Damascus
question: From whom had Saul received authority in Damascus to bind all who call on the Lord’s name?
explanation: Ananias points out that Saul “hath authority from the chief priests to bind all that call on thy name.”

subject: Andrew
question: What was the trade of Andrew and his brother Simon when Jesus called them?
explanation: Jesus saw Simon and Andrew “casting a net into the sea: for they were fishers.”

subject: Andrew
question: What did the boy whom Andrew pointed out before the feeding of the crowd have?
choice_a: Five barley loaves and two fish
choice_b: Seven loaves and a few small fish
choice_c: Two barley loaves and five fish
choice_d: Five wheat loaves and one fish
answer_text: Five barley loaves and two fish
explanation: Andrew said, “There is a lad here, which hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes.” The seven loaves belong to the other feeding (Matt 15:34).

subject: Hannah
question: What name did Hannah give her son?
