explanation: Hannah bore a son and “called his name Samuel, saying, Because I have asked him of the LORD.”

subject: Hannah
question: Who was Hannah’s rival, who provoked her every year?
explanation: Peninnah, Elkanah’s other wife, had children; whenever Hannah went up to the house of the LORD, “so she provoked her.”

subject: Apollos
question: What city was Apollos from?
explanation: The text introduces him this way: “a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, and mighty in the scriptures.”

subject: Apollos
question: Which name comes right after Apollos’s in the slogans of the divided Corinthians?
explanation: “I am of Paul; and I of Apollos; and I of Cephas; and I of Christ.” Cephas comes right after Apollos; Christ is named last.

subject: Balaam
question: Which animal stopped Balaam on the road when it saw the angel of the LORD?
explanation: “The ass saw the angel of the LORD standing in the way, and his sword drawn in his hand: and the ass turned aside out of the way.” Balaam himself could not see him.

subject: Balaam
question: How many altars did Balaam have built at each site?
explanation: “Build me here seven altars, and prepare me here seven oxen and seven rams.” He repeats the request on Pisgah and on Peor.

subject: Barnabas
question: Whom did Barnabas bring to the apostles when everyone was afraid of him?
explanation: They were all afraid of Saul, not believing he was a disciple; “but Barnabas took him, and brought him to the apostles.”

subject: Barnabas
question: At Lystra, what god’s name did the crowd give Barnabas?
explanation: “They called Barnabas, Jupiter; and Paul, Mercury, because he was the chief speaker.”

subject: Baruch
question: What was the name of the father of Baruch, Jeremiah’s scribe?
explanation: Jeremiah hands the deed “unto Baruch the son of Neriah, the son of Maaseiah”: Neriah is his father, Maaseiah his grandfather. Hilkiah was Jeremiah’s father.

subject: Baruch
question: In which year of Jehoiakim’s reign did Baruch write the scroll at Jeremiah’s dictation?
explanation: It was “in the fourth year of Jehoiakim” that the LORD told Jeremiah to take a scroll. The public reading came a year later, in the fifth year.

subject: Bathsheba
question: Which of David’s sons was anointed king at Gihon?
explanation: Zadok the priest took the horn of oil and “anointed Solomon”; the people shouted, “God save king Solomon.” Adonijah had only proclaimed himself king.

subject: Bathsheba
question: To whom did David send the letter ordering that Uriah be put in the thick of the fighting?
explanation: David wrote to Joab, and Uriah himself carried the letter: “Set ye Uriah in the forefront of the hottest battle… that he may be smitten, and die.”

subject: Boaz
question: Which town does Boaz live in?
explanation: Boaz “came from Bethlehem” and greeted his reapers: he is from Bethlehem of Judah, like the family of Elimelech.

subject: Boaz
question: How many of the city’s elders does Boaz take as witnesses at the gate?
explanation: Boaz “took ten men of the elders of the city” and told them to sit down: they would witness the matter of the redemption.

subject: Cain and Abel
question: What was Abel’s occupation?
explanation: “Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.” Work in bronze and iron would come later with Tubal-cain, a descendant of Cain.

subject: Cain and Abel
question: In which land did Cain settle after the murder?
explanation: “Cain went out from the presence of the LORD, and dwelt in the land of Nod, on the east of Eden.”

subject: Caiaphas
question: What office did Caiaphas hold?
explanation: Matthew speaks of “Caiaphas the high priest,” to whose house Jesus was taken after his arrest; John adds that he held the office “that same year.”

subject: Caiaphas
question: What charge did Caiaphas bring against Jesus after his answer?
explanation: Caiaphas tore his robes: “He hath spoken blasphemy… behold, now ye have heard his blasphemy.” The council answered, “He is guilty of death.”

subject: Caleb
question: Complete Caleb’s words: “Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to …”
explanation: Caleb told the grumbling people, “Let us go up at once, and possess it; for we are well able to overcome it.” The others answered that they could not go up.

subject: Caleb
question: Who captured Kiriath-sepher and received Achsah, Caleb’s daughter, as his wife?
explanation: “Othniel the son of Kenaz, the brother of Caleb, took it: and he gave him Achsah his daughter to wife.” He had won her hand by taking Debir.

subject: Cornelius
question: In which city did Cornelius live?
explanation: “There was a certain man in Caesarea called Cornelius.” Peter was staying in Joppa with Simon the tanner.

subject: Cornelius
question: According to the angel, what had come up before God as a memorial?
explanation: The angel said, “Thy prayers and thine alms are come up for a memorial before God.” Cornelius gave much in alms and prayed continually.

subject: Cyrus
question: What did Cyrus say he was charged to build in Jerusalem?
explanation: Cyrus proclaims that the LORD God of heaven “hath charged me to build him an house at Jerusalem, which is in Judah.”

subject: Cyrus
question: To whom did the treasurer Mithredath count out the vessels of the house of the LORD?
explanation: Cyrus had them brought out by Mithredath the treasurer, who “numbered them unto Sheshbazzar, the prince of Judah.”

subject: Daniel
question: How many times a day did Daniel pray, kneeling toward Jerusalem?
explanation: Despite the decree, “he kneeled upon his knees three times a day, and prayed, and gave thanks before his God, as he did aforetime.”

subject: Daniel
question: In the dream of the statue, what did the head of gold represent?
explanation: Daniel told the king, “Thou art this head of gold. And after thee shall arise another kingdom inferior to thee.”

subject: David
question: What was David doing when Samuel came to anoint one of Jesse’s sons?
explanation: Jesse answered Samuel, “There remaineth yet the youngest, and, behold, he keepeth the sheep.” They sent for him, and Samuel anointed him.

subject: David
question: What did David cut off from Saul in the cave at En-gedi?
explanation: “David arose, and cut off the skirt of Saul’s robe privily,” and afterward his heart smote him for laying a hand on the LORD’s anointed.

subject: Deborah
question: Which military leader did Deborah call to fight Sisera?
explanation: “She sent and called Barak the son of Abinoam out of Kedesh-naphtali” and relayed the LORD’s command to him.

subject: Deborah
question: How did Barak respond when Deborah relayed God’s command?
choice_b: “If thou wilt go with me, then I will go”
answer_text: “If thou wilt go with me, then I will go”
explanation: “If thou wilt go with me, then I will go: but if thou wilt not go with me, then I will not go.” Deborah then announced that Sisera would be sold into the hand of a woman.

subject: Eli
question: How does Eli die?
choice_b: He dies in his bed of old age
choice_c: Killed at Nob by Doeg’s sword
explanation: When he hears that the ark has been captured, Eli “fell from off the seat backward by the side of the gate, and his neck brake, and he died.”

subject: Eli
question: How old was Eli when he died?
explanation: Eli “was ninety and eight years old; and his eyes were dim, that he could not see.”

subject: Elijah
question: On which mountain did Elijah confront the prophets of Baal?
explanation: Elijah had all Israel and the prophets of Baal gather “unto mount Carmel.” He would later flee all the way to Horeb.

subject: Elijah
question: What did Elijah ask for as he sat under the broom tree?
choice_c: “It is enough; take away my life”
answer_text: “It is enough; take away my life”
explanation: He asked to die: “It is enough; now, O LORD, take away my life; for I am not better than my fathers.”

subject: Elisha
question: What did Elisha ask of Elijah before he was taken up?
choice_b: A double portion of his spirit
choice_d: The power to shut up the sky
answer_text: A double portion of his spirit
explanation: “I pray thee, let a double portion of thy spirit be upon me.” Elijah answered, “Thou hast asked a hard thing.”

subject: Elisha
question: What did Elisha throw into the spring to heal the waters of Jericho?
explanation: “Bring me a new cruse, and put salt therein”; Elisha cast the salt into the spring and said, “I have healed these waters.” The wood thrown into the water belongs to the story at Marah.

subject: Isaiah
question: How did Isaiah answer the question “Whom shall I send?”
explanation: “Whom shall I send, and who will go for us? Then said I, Here am I; send me.” The other answers recall the hesitations of Moses and Jeremiah.

subject: Isaiah
question: How many men did the angel of the LORD strike down in the Assyrian camp?
explanation: “The angel of the LORD went forth, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians a hundred and fourscore and five thousand.”

subject: Esau
question: What did Esau become as he grew up?
explanation: “Esau was a cunning hunter, a man of the field; and Jacob was a plain man, dwelling in tents.”

subject: Esau
question: Whom did Esau go to in order to marry Mahalath?
explanation: “Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took unto the wives which he had Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife.”

subject: Ezra
question: According to Ezra 7:10, to what had Ezra applied his heart?
choice_c: Raising up the altar of burnt offering
explanation: Ezra “had prepared his heart to seek the law of the LORD, and to do it, and to teach in Israel statutes and judgments.”

subject: Ezra
question: By which river did Ezra proclaim a fast before the journey?
explanation: “Then I proclaimed a fast there, at the river of Ahava, that we might afflict ourselves before our God, to seek of him a right way for us.”

subject: Esther
question: Which queen did Esther replace?
explanation: The king “set the royal crown upon her head, and made her queen instead of Vashti.” Hadassah is Esther’s other name, and Zeresh is Haman’s wife.

subject: Esther
question: What does the word “Pur,” which gave its name to the feast of Purim, mean?
explanation: Haman “had cast Pur, that is, the lot,” to set the day of the massacre; “wherefore they called these days Purim after the name of Pur.”

subject: Stephen
question: How did Stephen die?
explanation: They rushed at him, “cast him out of the city, and stoned him.” It was James whom Herod put to death.

subject: Stephen
question: In what position did Stephen see Jesus at the right hand of God?
explanation: Stephen “saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing on the right hand of God”: “Behold, I see the heavens opened, and the Son of man standing.”

subject: Hezekiah
question: Which king of Assyria came up against the fortified cities of Judah under Hezekiah?
explanation: “In the fourteenth year of king Hezekiah did Sennacherib king of Assyria come up against all the fenced cities of Judah, and took them.”

subject: Hezekiah
question: How many Assyrian soldiers did the angel of the LORD strike down in one night?
explanation: “That night… the angel of the LORD went out, and smote in the camp of the Assyrians an hundred fourscore and five thousand.”

subject: Ezekiel
question: Near which river did Ezekiel have his first visions?
explanation: “As I was among the captives by the river of Chebar, the heavens were opened, and I saw visions of God.”

subject: Ezekiel
question: Why did Ezekiel not mourn when his wife died?
choice_a: God had made it a sign
choice_b: He was mute and ill at the time
choice_d: He was in prison that day
answer_text: God had made it a sign
explanation: God had told him, “neither shalt thou mourn nor weep,” and told the people, “Ezekiel is unto you a sign: according to all that he hath done shall ye do.”

subject: Gideon
question: What was Gideon doing when the angel of the LORD appeared to him?
explanation: Gideon “threshed wheat by the winepress, to hide it from the Midianites” when the angel told him, “The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valor.”

subject: Gideon
question: In the second sign Gideon asked for, what stayed dry?
explanation: Gideon asked for the reverse of the first sign: “it was dry upon the fleece only, and there was dew on all the ground.”

subject: Enoch
question: Complete the verse: “Enoch walked with God: and he was not; for…”
explanation: Genesis 5:24 concludes, “for God took him.” Hebrews adds that he was taken up so that he would not see death.

subject: Enoch
question: According to Hebrews 11, what testimony did Enoch receive before he was taken up?
choice_a: That he was righteous in his generation
choice_b: That he was a blameless man
choice_d: That he was a friend of God
explanation: “Before his translation he had this testimony, that he pleased God.” “Just and perfect in his generations” is said of Noah, and “the friend of God” of Abraham.

subject: The Herods
question: What animal does Jesus use to describe Herod?
explanation: When Pharisees tell him that Herod wants to kill him, Jesus answers, “Go ye, and tell that fox, Behold, I cast out devils…”

subject: The Herods
question: Who was reigning over Judea “in the room of his father Herod” when Joseph came back from Egypt?
explanation: When Joseph heard that Archelaus was reigning over Judea in place of his father Herod, he was afraid to go there and turned aside to Galilee.

subject: Isaac
question: What was offered on the altar in Isaac’s place?
explanation: Abraham “looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in a thicket by his horns” and “offered him up for a burnt offering in the stead of his son.”

subject: Isaac
question: What name did Isaac give the well that no one fought over?
explanation: After Esek and Sitnah, which caused quarrels, Isaac dug another well: “he called the name of it Rehoboth; and he said, For now the LORD hath made room for us.”

subject: Jacob
question: How many years did Jacob serve Laban for his two wives?
explanation: “I served thee fourteen years for thy two daughters, and six years for thy cattle”: twenty years in all in Laban’s house.

subject: Jacob
question: Which river ford did Jacob send his family across on the night he wrestled until daybreak?
explanation: Jacob took his wives and children “and passed over the ford Jabbok”; then, left alone, he wrestled with a man until daybreak.

subject: James, son of Zebedee
question: What name did Jesus give to James and his brother John?
explanation: Jesus gave the two brothers “the name Boanerges, which is, The sons of thunder.” “Son of consolation” is the nickname of Barnabas.

subject: James, son of Zebedee
question: What did James and John propose when a Samaritan village refused to receive Jesus?
choice_b: Shaking the dust off their feet
explanation: They said, “Lord, wilt thou that we command fire to come down from heaven, and consume them?” Jesus rebuked them.

subject: James, the Lord’s brother
question: What was the attitude of Jesus’ brothers during his ministry?
choice_b: They did not believe in him
choice_c: They wanted to make him king
answer_text: They did not believe in him
explanation: John puts it plainly: “For neither did his brethren believe in him.”

subject: James, the Lord’s brother
question: What message did Peter, freed from prison, have passed on to James and the brothers?
choice_a: That he should leave Jerusalem without delay
choice_b: That the Lord had brought him out of prison
choice_c: That he should gather the elders
choice_d: That he should send Mark to Antioch
answer_text: That the Lord had brought him out of prison
explanation: Peter “declared unto them how the Lord had brought him out of the prison. And he said, Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren.”

subject: John the Baptist
question: In which river did John baptize the crowds?
explanation: The crowds came from Jerusalem and Judea, “and were baptized of him in Jordan, confessing their sins.”

subject: John the Baptist
question: Because of whom did Herod have John arrested?
explanation: Herod had bound him “for Herodias’ sake, his brother Philip’s wife,” because John told him, “It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother’s wife.”

subject: John the apostle
question: On which island did John receive the revelation of Revelation?
explanation: “I John, who also am your brother… was in the isle that is called Patmos, for the word of God, and for the testimony of Jesus Christ.”

subject: John the apostle
question: What words did Jesus speak to the disciple he loved from the cross?
explanation: Jesus said to his mother, “Woman, behold thy son!” and then to the disciple, “Behold thy mother! And from that hour that disciple took her unto his own home.”

subject: Jephthah
question: Against which people does Jephthah lead the Gileadites?
explanation: The Ammonites make war on Israel; Jephthah marches against them and “the LORD delivered them into his hands.” The Philistines had also oppressed Israel, but they are not the ones he fights.

subject: Jephthah
question: How much time does Jephthah’s daughter ask her father for before the vow is carried out?
explanation: “Let me alone two months!” She wants to go up and down the mountains and mourn her virginity with her companions; her father answers, “Go.”

subject: Jeremiah
question: What village was Jeremiah from?
explanation: Jeremiah was “the son of Hilkiah, of the priests that were in Anathoth in the land of Benjamin.”

subject: Jeremiah
question: What did King Jehoiakim do with the scroll written by Baruch?
choice_a: He had it hidden in the temple
choice_b: He burned it in the fire pot
choice_d: He threw it into the Euphrates
answer_text: He burned it in the fire pot
explanation: The king “cut it with the penknife, and cast it into the fire that was on the hearth, until all the roll was consumed.”

subject: Jeroboam I
question: To which country did Jeroboam flee to escape Solomon?
explanation: Solomon sought to kill him, so Jeroboam fled “unto Shishak king of Egypt” and stayed there until Solomon’s death.

subject: Jeroboam I
question: Whom did Jeroboam appoint as priests of the high places?
choice_b: Ordinary men from among the people
answer_text: Ordinary men from among the people
explanation: He made priests “of the lowest of the people, which were not of the sons of Levi.”

subject: Jesus Christ
question: In which town was Jesus born?
explanation: Joseph went up from Nazareth “unto the city of David, which is called Bethlehem,” and there Mary gave birth to her firstborn son.

subject: Jesus Christ
question: What does Jesus say, at age twelve, to his parents when they find him in the temple?
choice_a: “I must be about my Father’s business”
choice_b: “My Father worketh hitherto, and I work”
choice_c: “Woman, what have I to do with thee?”
choice_d: “I must work the works of him that sent me”
answer_text: “I must be about my Father’s business”
explanation: Found in the temple after three days, he says: “Wist ye not that I must be about my Father’s business?”

subject: Jethro
question: Which of the Midianite priest’s daughters did Moses marry?
explanation: The priest of Midian “gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.” Zilpah and Bilhah were the servants of Leah and Rachel.

subject: Jethro
question: What was the name of Moses’ second son, whom Jethro brought to the camp with his mother?
explanation: “The name of the other was Eliezer; for the God of my father, said he, was mine help.” Gershom was the first son; Eleazar and Ithamar were sons of Aaron.

subject: Jezebel
question: Which prophet did Jezebel threaten with death after Carmel?
explanation: Jezebel sent a messenger to Elijah: “So let the gods do to me, and more also, if I make not thy life as the life of one of them by to morrow about this time.”

subject: Jezebel
question: Whose seal did Jezebel use to seal the letters sent to the elders of Jezreel?
explanation: She “wrote letters in Ahab’s name, and sealed them with his seal.”

subject: Joab
question: What was the name of Joab’s mother?
explanation: Joab is the “son of Zeruiah,” David’s sister. Abigail, her other sister, was the mother of Amasa.

subject: Joab
question: How many darts did Joab thrust through Absalom’s heart?
explanation: Joab “took three darts in his hand, and thrust them through the heart of Absalom.” Ten young men then finished him off.

subject: Joash
question: For how many years was Joash hidden in the house of the LORD?
explanation: Joash “was with her hid in the house of the LORD six years,” while Athaliah reigned. Jehoiada acted in the seventh year.

subject: Joash
question: How old was Joash when he became king?
explanation: “Seven years old was Jehoash when he began to reign,” and he reigned forty years in Jerusalem. Sixteen was Uzziah’s age, and twelve was Manasseh’s.

subject: Job
question: In which land did Job live?
explanation: The book opens: “There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job.”

subject: Job
question: What limit did God set for Satan in the second trial?
explanation: Satan could touch his bone and his flesh, but the LORD added: “Behold, he is in thine hand; but save his life.”

subject: Jonah
question: Where did Jonah try to flee?
explanation: “Jonah rose up to flee unto Tarshish from the presence of the LORD”; he boarded a ship at Joppa.

subject: Jonah
question: What deadline did Jonah announce to the people of Nineveh?
explanation: Jonah cried out: “Yet forty days, and Nineveh shall be overthrown!” The three days refer to the size of the city, measured in days of walking.

subject: Jonathan
question: How does Scripture say Jonathan loved David?
explanation: “The soul of Jonathan was knit with the soul of David, and Jonathan loved him as his own soul.” David, for his part, will call him “my brother” at his death.

subject: Jonathan
question: Where did Jonathan go to David to strengthen his trust in God?
choice_b: To the wood in the wilderness of Ziph
answer_text: To the wood in the wilderness of Ziph
explanation: David was in the wilderness of Ziph, in a wood; Jonathan went to him and “strengthened his hand in God.”

subject: Jehoshaphat
question: With which king of Israel did Jehoshaphat form a marriage alliance?
explanation: Jehoshaphat had riches and honor in abundance, “and joined affinity with Ahab.”

subject: Jehoshaphat
question: Whom did Jehoshaphat place in front of the army to face Moab and Ammon?
explanation: He appointed singers who went out “before the army” praising the LORD: “Praise the LORD; for his mercy endureth for ever!”

subject: Joseph of Nazareth
question: What was Joseph’s trade, according to the people of Nazareth?
explanation: “Is not this the carpenter’s son?” ask the people of his hometown. Mark even reports that Jesus was called “the carpenter” (Mark 6:3).

subject: Joseph of Nazareth
question: Who was ruling Judea when they came back from Egypt, which made Joseph afraid to go there?
explanation: Joseph heard “that Archelaus did reign in Judea in the room of his father Herod”; he was afraid to go there and turned aside into Galilee.

subject: Joseph
question: What did the seven fat cows in Pharaoh’s dream represent?
explanation: “The seven good kine are seven years”: seven years of great plenty. It is the lean cows that announce the famine.

subject: Joseph
question: Which brother proposed selling Joseph rather than killing him?
explanation: “Judah said unto his brethren, What profit is it if we slay our brother?… Come, and let us sell him to the Ishmeelites.”

subject: Josiah
question: What did the high priest Hilkiah find in the temple?
explanation: Hilkiah told Shaphan the secretary, “I have found the book of the law in the house of the LORD.”

subject: Josiah
question: By burning bones on the altar at Bethel, Josiah fulfilled whose prophecy?
choice_b: The man of God from Judah
answer_text: The man of God from Judah
explanation: Josiah burned the bones “according to the word of the LORD which the man of God proclaimed,” the one “which came from Judah” and had cried out against the altar at Bethel.

subject: Joshua
question: Which city saw its walls fall down after seven days of marching around it?
explanation: The LORD told Joshua, “See, I have given into thine hand Jericho”; after one lap a day for six days and seven laps on the seventh, “the wall of the city shall fall down flat.”

subject: Joshua
question: Why was Israel defeated at Ai?
choice_a: Because Achan had taken plunder devoted to destruction
answer_text: Because Achan had taken plunder devoted to destruction
explanation: “Achan, the son of Carmi… took of the accursed thing: and the anger of the LORD was kindled against the children of Israel.”

subject: Judah
question: What animal does Jacob compare Judah to in his blessing?
explanation: “Judah is a lion’s whelp… he stooped down, he couched as a lion.” Benjamin is compared to a wolf, Issachar to a strong donkey, and Naphtali to a doe.

subject: Judah
question: What were the names of the twins Tamar bore to Judah?
explanation: Perez came out first, even though his brother’s hand had the scarlet thread; then Zerah came out. Hezron and Hamul were Perez’s sons.

subject: Judas Iscariot
question: By what sign did Judas point out Jesus to those who came to arrest him?
explanation: He had given them this signal: “Whomsoever I shall kiss, that same is he: hold him fast.” Then he said, “Hail, Rabbi!” and kissed him.

subject: Judas Iscariot
question: On what occasion did Judas complain that a perfume had not been sold for three hundred denarii?
choice_b: At a meal at Zacchaeus’s house
explanation: At Bethany, a supper was held for Jesus; Mary anointed his feet with pure nard, and Judas protested, “Why was not this ointment sold for three hundred pence?”

subject: Laban
question: Which daughter did Laban bring to Jacob on the wedding night?
explanation: “In the evening… he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him.” Jacob didn’t realize it until the next morning: “behold, it was Leah.”

subject: Laban
question: Which servant did Laban give to Rachel?
explanation: “Laban gave to Rachel his daughter Bilhah his handmaid to be her maid.” Zilpah, for her part, was given to Leah.

subject: Lazarus of Bethany
question: What village was Lazarus from?
explanation: “Now a certain man was sick, named Lazarus, of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha.”

subject: Lazarus of Bethany
question: What did Jesus order before calling Lazarus out of the tomb?
explanation: Jesus said, “Take ye away the stone.” Martha objected that he had been dead four days, but Jesus reminded her that if she believed, she would see the glory of God.

subject: Leah
question: How many sons did Leah herself bear to Jacob?
explanation: When Zebulun was born, Leah said, “I have born him six sons.” After that she bore a daughter, Dinah.

subject: Leah
question: What was the name of the servant Laban gave to Leah?
explanation: “Laban gave unto his daughter Leah Zilpah his maid for an handmaid.” Bilhah was given to Rachel.

subject: Lot
question: As far as which city did Lot pitch his tent after separating from Abram?
explanation: Abram lived in the land of Canaan, while Lot “dwelt in the cities of the plain, and pitched his tent toward Sodom.”

subject: Lot
question: What did Lot bake for the two angels in Sodom?
explanation: Lot “made them a feast, and did bake unleavened bread.” The tender calf, curds, and milk were the meal Abraham served at Mamre.

subject: Luke
question: To whom is the Gospel of Luke addressed?
explanation: The prologue is addressed to “most excellent Theophilus,” so that he may know “the certainty of those things” he has been taught. Acts is addressed to him as well.

subject: Luke
question: At whose house did Luke and his companions stay in Caesarea?
explanation: At Caesarea, they “entered into the house of Philip the evangelist, which was one of the seven; and abode with him.” Agabus came to find them there.

subject: Manasseh
question: Who was the father of Manasseh, king of Judah?
explanation: “Hezekiah slept with his fathers: and Manasseh his son reigned in his stead.” Manasseh rebuilt the high places his father had destroyed.

subject: Manasseh
question: Which king of Israel did Manasseh imitate in making an image of Asherah?
explanation: Manasseh “made a grove, as did Ahab king of Israel,” and raised up altars for Baal.

subject: Mark
question: Who took Mark with him and sailed for Cyprus after the disagreement with Paul?
explanation: “Barnabas took Mark, and sailed unto Cyprus.” Paul, for his part, chose Silas.

subject: Mark
question: Whom did Peter ask to be told of his deliverance, after he explained how the Lord had brought him out of prison?
explanation: Peter motioned for silence, described how he was freed, and said, “Go shew these things unto James, and to the brethren.” Then he departed to another place.

subject: Mordecai
question: In which city did Mordecai live at the time of the events in this book?
explanation: “Now in Shushan the palace there was a certain Jew, whose name was Mordecai”; he had been carried away from Jerusalem among the captives.

subject: Mordecai
question: Who sought to lay hands on the king, according to what Mordecai told Esther?
choice_a: Seven princes of Persia and Media
choice_c: Two eunuchs, keepers of the door
answer_text: Two eunuchs, keepers of the door
explanation: Bigthan and Teresh, two eunuchs who kept the door, sought to lay hands on Ahasuerus; Mordecai told Esther, who reported it to the king.

subject: Mary Magdalene
question: Whom does Mary first take the risen Jesus to be?
explanation: “She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith unto him, Sir, if thou have borne him hence, tell me where thou hast laid him.”

subject: Mary Magdalene
question: According to John, how many angels does Mary see in the sepulchre?
explanation: As she stooped down, she saw “two angels in white,” sitting one at the head and the other at the feet.

subject: Mary, mother of Jesus
question: What words show Mary finally accepting the angel’s message?
explanation: After asking, “How shall this be?”, Mary says, “Behold the handmaid of the Lord; be it unto me according to thy word.”

subject: Mary, mother of Jesus
question: Who tells Mary, “a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also”?
explanation: At the temple, “Simeon blessed them, and said unto Mary his mother… a sword shall pierce through thy own soul also.” Anna comes along only afterward.

subject: Martha and Mary of Bethany
question: What did Mary pour on Jesus’ feet?
explanation: Mary took a pound of very costly ointment of spikenard, anointed Jesus’ feet, and wiped them with her hair; the house was filled with the odor of the ointment.

subject: Martha and Mary of Bethany
question: How many more days did Jesus stay where he was after hearing that Lazarus was sick?
explanation: “When he had heard therefore that he was sick, he abode two days still in the same place where he was.” Yet Jesus loved Martha, her sister, and Lazarus.

subject: Matthew
question: What other name do Mark and Luke give Matthew?
explanation: Mark writes “Levi the son of Alphaeus sitting at the receipt of custom”: it is the same scene as Matt 9:9, where the man is called Matthew.

subject: Matthew
question: What statement did Jesus make to the Pharisees who criticized him for eating with tax collectors?
choice_a: He came to seek and to save that which was lost
choice_b: He came not to destroy the law, but to fulfill it
choice_c: He came to send fire on the earth
choice_d: He came to call sinners, not the righteous
answer_text: He came to call sinners, not the righteous
explanation: Jesus answers, “I came not to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” Seeking and saving the lost is said later, about Zacchaeus.

subject: Melchizedek
question: What did Abram give to Melchizedek?
explanation: “And he gave him tithes of all.” Abram’s allies Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre took their share of the spoils, but that is a different scene.

subject: Melchizedek
question: According to Hebrews 7, what does Melchizedek’s name mean first of all?
explanation: He is “first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace”: peace is the meaning of Salem, not of his name.

subject: Micah
question: Which cities does Micah’s prophecy concern?
explanation: Micah receives a prophecy “concerning Samaria and Jerusalem,” in the days of Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah, kings of Judah.

subject: Micah
question: According to the elders in Jeremiah 26, which king of Judah did not put Micah to death, but feared the LORD?
explanation: “Did Hezekiah king of Judah and all Judah put him at all to death? did he not fear the LORD, and besought the LORD?”

subject: Moses
question: What final plague does the LORD announce, after which Pharaoh will let Israel go?
explanation: “Yet will I bring one plague more upon Pharaoh, and upon Egypt; afterwards he will let you go hence”: “all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die.”

subject: Moses
question: How old was Moses when he spoke to Pharaoh?
explanation: “Moses was fourscore years old, and Aaron fourscore and three years old, when they spake unto Pharaoh.”

subject: Miriam
question: What instrument did Miriam the prophetess take in her hand after the crossing of the Red Sea?
explanation: “Miriam the prophetess, the sister of Aaron, took a timbrel in her hand; and all the women went out after her.”

subject: Miriam
question: Where did Miriam die and where was she buried?
explanation: “The people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.” Aaron would die later on Mount Hor.

subject: Naaman
question: What disease did Naaman, commander of the army of the king of Syria, have?
explanation: “He was also a mighty man in valour, but he was a leper”: despite his military glory and his master’s favor, Naaman carried a disease no man could cure.

subject: Naaman
question: Which rivers did Naaman consider better than all the waters of Israel?
explanation: In a fury, Naaman said, “Are not Abana and Pharpar, rivers of Damascus, better than all the waters of Israel?” He turned and went away in a rage.

subject: Naomi
question: To which country does the famine lead Elimelech and Naomi to move?
explanation: A certain man of Bethlehem in Judah went “to sojourn in the country of Moab, he, and his wife, and his two sons,” because of the famine.

subject: Naomi
question: At what time of year do Naomi and Ruth arrive in Bethlehem?
choice_a: At the beginning of barley harvest
choice_b: At the end of wheat harvest
choice_c: At the time of the grape harvest
choice_d: At the start of the rainy season
answer_text: At the beginning of barley harvest
explanation: They came to Bethlehem “in the beginning of barley harvest,” so Ruth could glean as soon as she arrived.

subject: Nathan
question: How did David respond when Nathan had rebuked him?
choice_b: You have no right over me!
choice_c: I have sinned against the LORD!
answer_text: I have sinned against the LORD!
explanation: “David said unto Nathan, I have sinned against the LORD.” Nathan answered that the LORD had put away his sin.

subject: Nathan
question: According to the word Nathan delivered to David, who would build the house of the LORD?
explanation: The LORD announces, “I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels… He shall build an house for my name.”

subject: Nathanael
question: Under what kind of tree had Jesus seen Nathanael?
explanation: Jesus said, “Before that Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.” Those words floored Nathanael.

subject: Nathanael
question: Besides “Son of God,” what title does Nathanael give Jesus?
explanation: Nathanael exclaims, “Rabbi, thou art the Son of God; thou art the King of Israel.” He also calls him “Rabbi.”

subject: Nebuchadnezzar
question: What did Nebuchadnezzar set up in the plain of Dura?
explanation: King Nebuchadnezzar made an image of gold and set it up in the plain of Dura, in the province of Babylon, and summoned all the officials to its dedication.

subject: Nebuchadnezzar
question: What name did Nebuchadnezzar give Mattaniah, Jehoiachin’s uncle, when he made him king?
explanation: “The king of Babylon made Mattaniah his father’s brother king in his stead, and changed his name to Zedekiah.”

subject: Nehemiah
question: What position did Nehemiah hold with King Artaxerxes?
explanation: “For I was the king’s cupbearer”: in the month of Nisan, Nehemiah took up the wine and gave it to the king.

subject: Nehemiah
question: How did the builders of the wall protect themselves during the work?
choice_a: They held a weapon in one hand
choice_d: They shut themselves in the temple
answer_text: They held a weapon in one hand
explanation: The builders “wrought in the work, and with the other hand held a weapon,” each with his sword girded at his side.

subject: Nicodemus
question: At what time of day did Nicodemus come to Jesus?
explanation: Nicodemus “came to Jesus by night.” John mentions it twice more, in chapters 7 and 19.

subject: Nicodemus
question: Why does Nicodemus recognize Jesus as a teacher come from God?
choice_a: Because of the miracles he performed
choice_b: Because of his birth in Bethlehem
choice_c: Because of his baptism by John
choice_d: Because of his teaching in the temple
answer_text: Because of the miracles he performed
explanation: “No man can do these miracles that thou doest, except God be with him.”

subject: Noah
question: What is the sign of God’s covenant with Noah?
explanation: “I do set my bow in the cloud, and it shall be for a token of a covenant between me and the earth.” Circumcision would be the sign given to Abraham.

subject: Noah
question: How old was Noah when the flood came upon the earth?
explanation: “Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.” He died later at nine hundred fifty.

subject: Hosea
question: What was the name of the prophet Hosea’s father?
explanation: The book opens with “the word of the LORD that came unto Hosea, the son of Beeri.” Elah was the father of King Hoshea, Nun of Joshua, and Joash of Jeroboam.

subject: Hosea
question: Where does the LORD say he called his son out of, when Israel was a child?
explanation: “When Israel was a child, then I loved him, and called my son out of Egypt.” Matthew quotes these words about Jesus.

subject: Uzziah
question: What did Uzziah try to do in the temple that drew a rebuke?
choice_b: Offer a burnt offering of bulls
explanation: Uzziah went into the temple “to burn incense upon the altar of incense,” a right that belonged to the priests, the sons of Aaron.

subject: Uzziah
question: How many years did Uzziah reign in Jerusalem?
explanation: Uzziah “reigned fifty and two years in Jerusalem.” Forty years was the length of Joash’s reign, and fifty-five that of Manasseh’s.

subject: Paul
question: In which city was Paul born?
explanation: Paul declares, “I am verily a man which am a Jew, born in Tarsus, a city in Cilicia, yet brought up in this city,” that is, Jerusalem.

subject: Paul
question: Who accompanies Paul in the prison at Philippi, where they sing at midnight?
explanation: “At midnight Paul and Silas prayed, and sang praises unto God: and the prisoners heard them.”

subject: Philip the Evangelist
question: In which city did Philip preach Christ after the persecution that followed Stephen’s death?
explanation: “Then Philip went down to the city of Samaria, and preached Christ unto them.” The crowds listened, for they saw the miracles he did.

subject: Philip the Evangelist
question: Who said to Philip, “Go near, and join thyself to this chariot”?
explanation: It is “the Spirit” who speaks to Philip; an angel of the Lord had first sent him onto the Gaza road (8:26).

subject: Philip
question: What town was Philip from?
explanation: “Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.” Nathanael, by contrast, was from Cana in Galilee.

subject: Philip
question: What sum did Philip cite when faced with the crowd to be fed?
explanation: Philip answered, “Two hundred pennyworth of bread is not sufficient for them, that every one of them may take a little.”

subject: Phinehas
question: How many people died in the plague that struck Israel at Shittim?
explanation: “Those that died in the plague were twenty and four thousand.” It was stayed when Phinehas stepped in.

subject: Phinehas
question: What was the name of the Israelite whom Phinehas ran through along with the Midianite woman?
explanation: “The name of the Israelite that was slain, even that was slain with the Midianitish woman, was Zimri, the son of Salu”; he was a prince of a chief house among the Simeonites.

subject: Peter
question: Who brought Simon Peter to Jesus?
explanation: Andrew first found his own brother Simon: “We have found the Messiah,” “and he brought him to Jesus.”

subject: Peter
question: What was the name of the high priest’s servant whose ear Peter cut off?
explanation: Simon Peter drew his sword and cut off his right ear. “The servant’s name was Malchus.”

subject: Pontius Pilate
question: What did Pilate do in front of the crowd to show he was innocent of Jesus’ blood?
explanation: Pilate “took water, and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am innocent of the blood of this just person: see ye to it.”

subject: Pontius Pilate
question: To whom did Pilate send Jesus when he learned that he was a Galilean?
explanation: Having learned that Jesus belonged to Herod’s jurisdiction, and that Herod was also in Jerusalem, Pilate sent him to Herod.

subject: Priscilla and Aquila
question: What was the trade of Priscilla and Aquila?
explanation: Paul, who shared their trade, “abode with them, and wrought: for by their occupation they were tentmakers.”

subject: Priscilla and Aquila
question: What region was Aquila from?
explanation: In Corinth, Paul found “a certain Jew named Aquila, born in Pontus.” Cilicia was Paul’s home region.

subject: Rachel
question: How many years did Jacob offer to serve Laban to win Rachel?
explanation: Jacob said, “I will serve thee seven years for Rachel thy younger daughter.” Deceived by Laban, he then had to serve seven more years.

subject: Rachel
question: Where did Rachel hide the household idols she had stolen from her father?
explanation: Rachel had “put them in the camel’s furniture, and sat upon them”; Laban searched the whole tent and found nothing.

subject: Rahab
question: Where did Rahab hide the spies?
choice_c: In the cellar of her house
explanation: “She had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof.”

subject: Rahab
question: For how many days did Rahab advise the spies to hide in the hills?
explanation: “Hide yourselves there three days, until the pursuers be returned: and afterward may ye go your way.”

subject: Rebekah
question: What did Rebekah do to answer the sign the servant had asked for?
choice_a: She gave his camels water too
choice_c: She prepared a meal for him
choice_d: She led him to her father’s house
answer_text: She gave his camels water too
explanation: She said, “I will draw water for thy camels also, until they have done drinking.” This was the sign the servant had asked of the LORD (Gen 24:14).

subject: Rebekah
question: How old was Isaac when he took Rebekah as his wife?
explanation: “Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife.” He will be sixty when Esau and Jacob are born.

subject: Rehoboam
question: Which counselors did Rehoboam set aside before answering the people?
explanation: Rehoboam “forsook the counsel of the old men” who had served Solomon, and consulted the young men who had grown up with him.

subject: Rehoboam
question: Which king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem in Rehoboam’s fifth year?
explanation: “In the fifth year of king Rehoboam, Shishak king of Egypt came up against Jerusalem” and took the treasures of the temple and the palace.

subject: Ruth
question: What was the name of Ruth’s mother-in-law?
explanation: Elimelech’s wife was Naomi; their sons married Orpah and Ruth, who thus became her daughters-in-law.

subject: Ruth
question: What gesture confirmed the nearest relative’s renunciation?
explanation: To confirm a redemption, “a man plucked off his shoe, and gave it to his neighbour”; the relative told Boaz, “Buy it for thee. So he drew off his shoe.”

subject: Solomon
question: What did Solomon ask of God at Gibeon?
explanation: “Give therefore thy servant an understanding heart to judge thy people.” God notes that he asked neither for long life, nor for riches, nor for the life of his enemies.

subject: Solomon
question: What name did the prophet Nathan give Solomon?
explanation: David sent the child by the hand of Nathan the prophet, “and he called his name Jedidiah, because of the LORD.”

subject: Samson
question: Why was a razor never to touch Samson’s head?
choice_a: He would be the king of Israel
choice_c: He would be consecrated to God
answer_text: He would be consecrated to God
explanation: The angel announces, “no razor shall come on his head: for the child shall be a Nazarite unto God from the womb.”

subject: Samson
question: Where did Samson carry the gates of Gaza?
choice_a: To the top of a hill facing Hebron
answer_text: To the top of a hill facing Hebron
explanation: He put the doors, the posts and the bar on his shoulders, “and carried them up to the top of an hill that is before Hebron.”

subject: Samuel
question: What did Samuel answer at God’s last call in the night?
choice_a: “Here am I; for thou didst call me”
explanation: The LORD called, “Samuel, Samuel.” “Then Samuel answered, Speak; for thy servant heareth.” “Here am I” was his answer to Eli.

subject: Samuel
question: What does the stone Ebenezer mean, according to Samuel?
choice_b: “God hath made me forget all my toil”
explanation: Samuel set a stone between Mizpeh and Shen, “and called the name of it Eben-ezer, saying, Hitherto hath the LORD helped us.”

subject: Sarah
question: What was the name of Sarah’s Egyptian servant?
explanation: Sarai “had an handmaid, an Egyptian, whose name was Hagar.” Bilhah and Zilpah were the servants of Rachel and Leah.

subject: Sarah
question: According to Abraham, how old was Sarah when God promised him a son by her?
explanation: Abraham laughed and said in his heart, “Shall a child be born unto him that is an hundred years old? and shall Sarah, that is ninety years old, bear?”

subject: Saul
question: Which tribe was Saul from?
explanation: “There was a man of Benjamin, whose name was Kish… And he had a son, whose name was Saul, a choice young man, and a goodly.”

subject: Saul
question: What sin did Saul commit at Gilgal while waiting for Samuel?
explanation: Seeing the people scatter, Saul “offered a burnt offering” rather than wait for Samuel, who told him, “thy kingdom shall not continue.”

subject: Silas
question: Whom did Paul choose to accompany him after parting ways with Barnabas?
explanation: “Paul chose Silas, and departed, being recommended by the brethren unto the grace of God.” Barnabas, for his part, took Mark with him to Cyprus.

subject: Silas
question: What does the text call Judas and Silas when they strengthen the brothers in Antioch?
explanation: “Judas and Silas, being prophets also themselves, exhorted the brethren with many words, and confirmed them.” The apostles and elders were the ones who had sent them.

subject: Thomas
question: What did Thomas say when he saw the risen Jesus?
choice_a: Rabbi, thou art the Son of God
choice_b: Thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God
explanation: Thomas answered, “My Lord and my God!” “Rabbi, thou art the Son of God” is what Nathanael said, and “Thou art the Christ” is what Peter said.

subject: Thomas
question: What condition did Thomas set for believing in the resurrection?
choice_a: To see the empty tomb and the grave clothes
choice_b: To hear Jesus call him by name
choice_c: To see and touch the marks of the nails
choice_d: To see Jesus eat in front of all the disciples
answer_text: To see and touch the marks of the nails
explanation: He said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails… and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” The empty tomb was what Peter had seen.

subject: Timothy
question: What were the names of Timothy’s mother and grandmother?
explanation: Paul speaks of the unfeigned faith “which dwelt first in thy grandmother Lois, and thy mother Eunice.”

subject: Timothy
question: In which city did Paul leave Timothy to stand against false teachers?
explanation: “I besought thee to abide still at Ephesus, when I went into Macedonia, that thou mightest charge some that they teach no other doctrine.”

subject: Titus
question: According to Galatians 2:1, which companion did Paul have with him in Jerusalem besides Titus?
explanation: “Then fourteen years after I went up again to Jerusalem with Barnabas, and took Titus with me also.”

subject: Titus
question: What was Titus to appoint in every city of Crete, according to Paul’s instructions?
explanation: Paul left him in Crete so that he would “ordain elders in every city, as I had appointed thee.”

subject: Zechariah and Elizabeth
question: What name did the angel tell Zechariah to give his son?
explanation: The angel said, “Thy wife Elisabeth shall bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.” Zechariah was his father’s name, and Jesus is the name Gabriel would announce to Mary.

subject: Zechariah and Elizabeth
question: What was Zechariah doing in the temple when the angel appeared to him?
explanation: The lot had fallen to him “to burn incense when he went into the temple of the Lord,” and the angel stood on the right side of the altar of incense.

subject: Zacchaeus
question: What kind of tree did Zacchaeus climb to see Jesus?
explanation: Zacchaeus “ran before, and climbed up into a sycomore tree,” because the crowd and his short stature kept him from seeing Jesus, who was to pass that way.

subject: Zacchaeus
question: What did Jesus say to Zacchaeus when he looked up at him?
explanation: Jesus said to him, “Zaccheus, make haste, and come down; for to day I must abide at thy house.” He calls him by name before anything else.

subject: Zerubbabel
question: Which high priest led the work with Zerubbabel?
explanation: Zerubbabel the son of Shealtiel and Jeshua the son of Jozadak rose up and began to build the house of God at Jerusalem.

subject: Zerubbabel
question: What did Zerubbabel and Joshua rebuild first, in the seventh month?
choice_b: The altar of the God of Israel
answer_text: The altar of the God of Israel
explanation: They rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel to offer burnt offerings on it; “the foundation of the temple of the LORD was not yet laid.”

subject: Hosea and Gomer
question: Where does the LORD say he will lead his unfaithful wife so he can speak to her heart?
explanation: “I will allure her, and bring her into the wilderness, and speak comfortably unto her”: God gently brings back the one he had disciplined.

subject: Martha and Mary
question: What does Mary do while Martha is busy serving?
choice_a: She pours perfume on his feet
choice_b: She helps Martha serve the meal
choice_c: She sits at his feet and listens to his word
choice_d: She goes to fetch water from the well
answer_text: She sits at his feet and listens to his word
explanation: Mary, who “also sat at Jesus’ feet, and heard his word,” while Martha was cumbered about much serving.

subject: The Angel Announces John’s Birth to Zechariah
question: What is Zechariah doing when the angel appears to him?
choice_c: Reading the Law to the assembly
explanation: Zechariah was carrying out his priestly duties: his lot was to go into the temple of the Lord and burn incense.

subject: Jesus Drives the Merchants from the Temple
question: What does Jesus use to drive the merchants out of the temple?
explanation: “When he had made a scourge of small cords, he drove them all out of the temple, and the sheep, and the oxen”; then he overturned the tables.

subject: The Demon-Possessed Man of Gadara
question: What name does the unclean spirit give when Jesus asks for its name?
explanation: When asked, “What is your name?” he answers: “My name is Legion: for we are many.”

subject: Blind Bartimaeus
question: What title does Bartimaeus use for Jesus as he cries out to him?
explanation: Hearing that it is Jesus of Nazareth, Bartimaeus cries out, “Jesus, thou Son of David, have mercy on me.”

subject: Jesus Heals the Royal Official’s Son
question: What words does Jesus speak to the official to announce the healing?
explanation: “Go thy way,” Jesus tells him, “thy son liveth.” The man believed the word that Jesus had spoken and went his way, with Jesus never leaving Cana.

subject: Samson
question: Who gets Samson to reveal the secret of his strength?
explanation: Pressed day after day, Samson “told her all his heart”: “There hath not come a razor upon mine head.” Delilah immediately called for the Philistine lords.

subject: David and Bathsheba
question: Who was Bathsheba’s husband?
explanation: Someone answers David: “Is not this Bath-sheba, the daughter of Eliam, the wife of Uriah the Hittite?”

subject: Hagar and the God Who Sees
question: Where does the angel of the LORD find Hagar after she runs away?
choice_b: By a spring in the wilderness
choice_c: At the foot of Mount Horeb
answer_text: By a spring in the wilderness
explanation: “The angel of the LORD found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain in the way to Shur.”

subject: Achan’s Sin and the Capture of Ai
question: To which valley is Achan taken to be stoned?
explanation: Joshua and all Israel bring Achan, along with all that belonged to him, to the valley of Achor; the place keeps that name “unto this day.”

subject: Manasseh’s Repentance
question: How old is Manasseh when he becomes king?
explanation: “Manasseh was twelve years old when he began to reign, and he reigned fifty and five years in Jerusalem.” He did evil in the sight of the LORD.
